### 40.Fuel Filter

A: REMOVAL

WARNING: Place “NO OPEN FLAMES” signs near the working area.

CAUTION:

• Be careful not to spill fuel.
• If the fuel gauge indicates that two thirds or more of the fuel is remaining, be sure to drain fuel before starting work to avoid the fuel to spill.
• Be careful not to drop or apply any impact to the fuel pump during work. This may deteriorate its performance.

NOTE:

The fuel filter is built in fuel pump assembly.

1) Remove the fuel pump assembly. <Ref. to FU(H4DOTC)-178, REMOVAL, Fuel Pump.>
2) Remove the fuel level sensor. <Ref. to FU(H4DOTC)-184, REMOVAL, Fuel Level Sensor.>
3) Remove the connector cable from the clip, and disconnect the connector (A) of the connector cable.

![](images/d792d6532bc9e029394b086ece75871aa2dc7e89b88c49b55208fe0b580f5405.jpg)

FU-07677

4) Push the fuel filter assembly in the direction of the arrow to compress, and detach the connecting clip.

![](images/648ef6cbe5735f1ea5b947fd3e7c86d6c5986fa07561ee9ca23f17fbf1291db2.jpg)

### Fuel Filter

5) Release the claw using a flat tip screwdriver or similar tool wrapped with a protection tape, and remove the tube assembly from the fuel chamber assembly.

![](images/53bf028959de5b53b9cbe6117b69106afa825ffd4182592af3aa851de3dd75b5.jpg)

6) Release three claws on the fuel pump holder from the fuel chamber assembly, and raise the fuel filter assembly.

![](images/0aa15d24f00f6326b7a9de9e3a7385e797e32aac4c41112b1435a59eac602c8e.jpg)

7) Using a flat tip screwdriver or similar tool wrapped with a protection tape, remove the tube assembly from the fuel chamber assembly, and separate the fuel filter assembly and fuel chamber assembly.

![](images/3516c4cd37c9e3fa608eb6a1e33ac2c9e539950bf55e6025f0baf593939d1286.jpg)

8) Using a precision driver or similar tool wrapped with a protection tape, expand the claws on the fuel pump.

### 41.Fuel Delivery and Evaporation Lines

A: REMOVAL

![](images/38001dee579de82121f4232d1faea98200b8553946d22c8f5d56b9add64b8edf.jpg)

WARNING:

Place “NO OPEN FLAMES” signs near the working area.

CAUTION: Be careful not to spill fuel.

1) Release the fuel pressure. <Ref. to FU(H4DOTC)-151, RELEASING OF FUEL PRESSURE, PROCEDURE, Fuel.>
2) Open the fuel filler lid and remove the fuel filler cap.
3) Remove the floor mat. <Ref. to EI-124, REMOVAL, Floor Mat.>

4) In the engine compartment, disconnect the fuel delivery tube (A) and evaporation hose (B). CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill fuel.
Catch the fuel from the tubes using a container or cloth.

NOTE: Disconnect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/023fd9e0323c67850978aa568eaf4e5947c8b2450ce78f4604a0faabf194b0a6.jpg)

(a) Slider

![](images/b41e25ac1f3c25255d291a341c0e50c62f633c672c9e994d81b298f46d3464d8.jpg)

5) Remove the fuel tank. <Ref. to FU(H4DOTC)-156, REMOVAL, Fuel Tank.>

6) Disconnect the quick connector, and remove the fuel delivery tube and jet pump tube from the fuel tank. CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill fuel.
Catch the fuel from the tubes using a container or cloth.

NOTE: Disconnect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/46886a42949ee9f92f362d217735e9d141b14338db2cbcdcb96ed3d9e0947513.jpg)

(a) Slider

7) Disconnect the quick connector and remove the purge pipe. NOTE: Disconnect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/e66528be2ab3883002445b10361c24d5bfec6bb5e7054486c9df3dd2c0a80a78.jpg)

8) Remove the body integrated unit.

(1) Remove the knee airbag module. <Ref. to AB-39, REMOVAL, Knee Airbag Module.> (2) Release the lock and remove the fuse holder from the relay & fuse box.

![](images/d1257dfe6f52fb39f7f1c873b3287dec949d0313503b690e9d1a2893975a8dac.jpg)

(3) Disconnect the connectors from the relay & fuse box.
(4) Remove the bolts (A) and nuts (B), and remove the relay & fuse box.

![](images/9b0266979626d61416d40140f7f1f1ce9e24f6866e45f521aebbb9911f69477c.jpg)

(5) Release the lock and remove the relay block.

![](images/4e4221b4bf468e1246b0260810dbf4468f6e078b0b44886836d5bc4e733ddff7.jpg)

(6) Disconnect the connector from body integrated unit.
(7) Remove the bolt (A) and nut (B), and remove the body integrated unit along with the bracket.

![](images/4e256c2dc16e68515d0d8e599482463105722024bd171a935ee15d24d893eb90.jpg)

9) Remove the fuel pipe assembly from vehicle.

### 1. CONNECTING THE EVAPORATION LINE QUICK CONNECTOR

NOTE: Connect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

CAUTION:

• Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. If necessary, clean the seal surface
of the pipe. Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

![](images/788e9a9d2e8b0036118a3360814c9b7d6027a31801a6501ab4fcfa26e600a3b7.jpg)

FU(H4DOTC)-211

### 2. CONNECTING THE FUEL LINE QUICK CONNECTOR

Connect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

CAUTION:

• Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. If necessary, clean the seal surface
of the pipe.
• When connecting the quick connector, make sure to insert the pipe all the way in before locking the
slider. When it is difficult to lock the slider, check that the pipe is fully inserted. Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

![](images/8e08225b5942a1e23d95466f14b41e6dc06e1c431782fd9258d08218c91f3683.jpg)

(a) Slider

### 3. EVAPORATION HOSE CONNECTION

Connect the evaporation hose by inserting it to the pipe until the hose reaches the spool or bump. NOTE: If there is no spool nor bump, connect the evaporation hose by inserting it at 2.8 mm (1.1 in) to the pipe.

![](images/ab1c472f074b6c1d2168a22ad6505339fa4cf5f4f0d9d0c2a313b51b33a10fcb.jpg)

FU-06185

### 4. BODY INTEGRATED UNIT INSTALLATION

Tighten the bolts and nuts in the figure to the torque specified below.

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/2e573264da09835b3567665e1c549c70b0dce74f3be2677a73aaed257ff51617.jpg)

### C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the fuel pipe has no deformation, cracks or other damages.
2) Check that the hose and tube have no cracks, damage or loose part.

### 42.Fuel System Trouble in General A: INSPECTION

![](images/60a2583d06773ba0307142697030d5954c22438d7786c77ac32664521aea194f.jpg)

NOTE:

• When the vehicle is left unattended for an extended period of time, water may accumulate in the fuel tank.
Fill fuel fully to prevent the problem.

• In snow-covered areas, mountainous areas, skiing areas, etc. where ambient temperatures drop to 0°C (32°F) or less throughout the winter season, use a water removing agent in the fuel system to prevent freezing fuel system and accumulating water.

When water is accumulated in fuel filter, fill the water removing agent in the fuel tank.
Before using water removing agent, follow the cautions noted on the bottle.

### B: CAUTION

Prior to starting work, pay special attention to the following:

1. Always wear work clothes, a safety cap, protective shoes. Additionally, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary. 2. Protect the vehicle using a seat cover, fender cover, etc. 3. Prepare the service tools, clean cloth, containers to catch grease and oil, etc.
• Vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated
parts.
• When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and
replacement.
• Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery.
• Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle.
• Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation, disassembly or assembly. Keep the removed parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.
• All removed parts, if to be reused, should be reinstalled in the original positions with attention to the correct
directions, etc. Bolts, nuts and washers should be replaced with new parts as required. Be sure to tighten the fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

### 2. Front Catalytic Converter

A: REMOVAL

The front catalytic converter is integrated into the center exhaust pipe (front). Refer to “Center Exhaust Pipe” for removal procedures. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-30, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>

### B: INSTALLATION

The front catalytic converter is integrated into the center exhaust pipe (front). Refer to “Center Exhaust Pipe” for installation procedures. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-35, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.>

### C: INSPECTION

1) Check the connections and welded parts for exhaust leaks.
2) Make sure there are no holes or rusting.

EC(H4DOTC)-6

### 3. Rear Catalytic Converter

A: REMOVAL

The rear catalytic converter is integrated into the center exhaust pipe (rear). Refer to “Center Exhaust Pipe” for removal procedures. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-30, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>

### B: INSTALLATION

The rear catalytic converter is integrated into the center exhaust pipe (rear). Refer to “Center Exhaust Pipe” for installation procedures. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-35, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.>

### C: INSPECTION

1) Check the connections and welded parts for exhaust leaks.
2) Make sure there are no holes or rusting.

EC(H4DOTC)-7

### A: REMOVAL

1) Lift up the vehicle.
2) Remove the rear exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-45, REMOVAL, Rear Exhaust Pipe.>
3) Remove the propeller shaft. <Ref. to DS-11, REMOVAL, Propeller Shaft.>
4) Support the rear differential with the transmission jack.
5) Remove the self-locking nuts which hold the rear differential to the rear sub frame assembly.

![](images/42ead3503de3f90da46436a478465a2afcac3b585d4e07d0a72e24305126e3f5.jpg)

6) Remove the rear differential member from the rear sub frame assembly and the rear differential.

![](images/8e0b7595026da5e451bd30a3ef11ff09b97a5a562c62771f17a963ce86c491d8.jpg)

### EC(H4DOTC)-8

7) Lower the transmission jack gradually until the rear differential is at the position shown in the figure. NOTE:

• When pulling out the stud bolt from the bushing portion of the rear sub frame assembly, adjust the angle and location of transmission jack and jack stand.

![](images/b83845666bdd9f902a7f33b5812bb55040f37b4ebadfc592cc82ae0ad6c88d62.jpg)

Do not lower the rear differential excessively. Doing so may add extra load to the drive shaft or cause the falling-off of the drive shaft.

![](images/8c200029d9df0ad5fab1203c0e28f9b3a30ada864c5771971c5e7b059fc3ad30.jpg)

### EC(H4DOTC)-9

8) Disconnect the drain tube (A), vent tube (B) and purge tube (C) from the canister. NOTE:
Disconnect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/3c95116b684b56d6f266af66a756da3406b17fab11bfbf132fc9902716bf667d.jpg)

EC-02971

(a) Drain tube and vent tube (b) Purge tube

![](images/2e156fe79b4e01eb0493c32043894b54ba0db3f609b6ebb74f28bea1b523f111.jpg)

9) Remove the canister from vehicle.

![](images/6d1109b2e350c23a679eb9a457f120aed41c737e8452c06f7a884ffff2a81ca2.jpg)

1) Install the canister to the vehicle.

>
> 3) Lift up the transmission jack gradually, and set the rear differential to the rear sub frame assembly. NOTE:
>
> When inserting the stud bolt into the bushing portion of the rear sub frame assembly, adjust the angle and location of transmission jack and jack stand.
>
> ![](images/12417dc4b294f5f2604e8d0a6605b535da8beca48844e37814e6331e368e6d69.jpg)

> 4) Temporarily tighten the self-locking nuts which hold the rear differential to the rear sub frame assembly. NOTE:

### 6. EGR Pipe

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/04fa890c4178811bd7e445a7b70bff6a4d587730c6bc11a0bef534ddeee590ab.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Remove the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-35, REMOVAL, Intercooler.>
4) Remove the clip securing the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold, and move the brake booster vacuum hose at the locations that do not interfere operation.

![](images/93015dc7aa3d82637c636c486d4fb71ba48e0dae96a577488414aaae51ab09d4.jpg)

5) Remove the bolts which secure the EGR pipe to the intake manifold and EGR control valve, and remove the EGR pipe.

![](images/46c2ac366c204c6543cbbb32cc6da48b0416086918b23aad44048def4121c4a3.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the EGR pipe to the intake manifold and EGR control valve. (1) Set the EGR pipe to the intake manifold and EGR control valve, and temporarily tighten the bolts which secure the EGR pipe to the intake manifold and EGR control valve.

NOTE: Use new gaskets and O-rings.

![](images/d98471b117a0e5fd40708ba5ef58f394d2c73425c71d858e5afe755167a755a9.jpg)

### EC(H4DOTC)-27

(2) Tighten the bolts which secure the EGR pipe to the intake manifold and EGR control valve in numerical order as shown in the figure.

Tightening torque: 19 N·m (1.9 kgf-m, 14.0 ft-lb)

![](images/a5b9236789f4a0d6f9d058b761b3b923320d9670dd66d70aa81112ad2be8e03e.jpg)

2) Install the clip which secures the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold.

![](images/be6a48d803b43752019f09c5e1d4effee492714127a0f0fef3983aa9ee287eeb.jpg)

3) Install the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-37, INSTALLATION, Intercooler.>
4) Connect the battery ground terminal.
5) Install the collector cover.

### 7. EGR Control Valve

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/bbedf4fd28fe59354e7d45cf35d144076ea84dd168774b4ed3cbebdb9c9de27f.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Lift up the vehicle.
4) Remove the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.>
5) Drain approximately 3.0 L (3.2 US qt, 2.6 Imp qt) of coolant. <Ref. to CO(H4DOTC)-13, DRAINING OF ENGINE COOLANT, REPLACEMENT, Engine Coolant.>
6) Remove the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-35, REMOVAL, Intercooler.>
7) Remove the EGR pipe. <Ref. to EC(H4DOTC)-26, REMOVAL, EGR Pipe.>
8) Remove the bolts which secure the EGR cooler to the EGR control valve, and remove the bolts which secure the EGR control valve bracket A to the EGR control valve bracket B.

![](images/c0ae3efcb0c53537583ed32133b3df2d9312cd37c3708cff104985e07522ed19.jpg)

9) Disconnect the connector (A) and preheater hose (B) from EGR control valve, and remove the EGR con trol valve.

![](images/513f6f7d7e373e4e25cdb7415ef6915cc440a6cde87cc08696618c69d5249860.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Connect the preheater hose (B) and connector (A) to the EGR control valve.

![](images/4115330848d4e065dc69a5184f8695347584d3889147ae764ea47c5217e8a3f8.jpg)

2) Install the EGR control valve and EGR control valve bracket A to the EGR cooler and EGR control valve
bracket B. (1) Set the EGR control valve and EGR control valve bracket A to the EGR cooler and EGR control valve bracket B, and temporarily tighten the bolts which secure the EGR control valve and EGR control valve bracket A to the EGR cooler and EGR control valve bracket B.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

![](images/69d56100d5f416d2cc1a9e5c13628a5bb03a433fe38bd87a84644e81f7eb04c8.jpg)

(2) Tighten the bolts which secure the EGR control valve and EGR control valve bracket A to the EGR cooler and EGR control valve bracket B in numerical order as shown in the figure.

Tightening torque: T1: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb) T2: 19 N·m (1.9 kgf-m, 14.0 ft-lb)

![](images/65c1c0ae3d73f77de2323f9578634c3409b64a315f8d7ea0a66601be7ef4948d.jpg)

3) Install the EGR pipe. <Ref. to EC(H4DOTC)-27, INSTALLATION, EGR Pipe.>
4) Install the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-37, INSTALLATION, Intercooler.>
5) Lift up the vehicle.
6) Install the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, INSTALLATION, Front Under Cover.>
7) Lower the vehicle.

### EC(H4DOTC)-31

8) Connect the battery ground terminal.
9) Fill engine coolant. <Ref. to CO(H4DOTC)-14, FILLING OF ENGINE COOLANT, REPLACEMENT, Engine Coolant.>
10) Install the collector cover.

### C: DISASSEMBLY

Remove the EGR control valve bracket A from the EGR control valve.

![](images/75cb194ec356429c23a026bf7f5de1d3f4d4cc5a23593bb264436ad12e95c802.jpg)

EC-03138

### E: INSPECTION

1) Check that the EGR control valve and EGR control valve bracket A have no deformation, cracks or other damages.
2) Measure the resistance between EGR control valve terminals.

![](images/78f11beaf24c47e5b4c9fba6f7bcf7d6a417570c912d6d46355a9f3c404a9ae6.jpg)

![](images/5df4318e38ffcd25008c1d0b90cdd8cb5393553c685b1b742dfcb10d60ef9070.jpg)

EC(H4DOTC)-33

### 8. EGR Cooler

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/42b752a1955f9b3d9826f1329b701b855490fca02cabbbc456a4fcfe62e685e1.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Remove the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-35, REMOVAL, Intercooler.>
4) Remove the clip securing the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold, and move the brake booster vacuum hose at the locations that do not interfere operation. 5) Lift up the vehicle.
6) Drain engine coolant. <Ref. to CO(H4DOTC)-13, DRAINING OF ENGINE COOLANT, REPLACEMENT, Engine Coolant.>

![](images/0a8c7e9b373c7462361f2f214b923a4eeedc346634ed1f5a30c6aa61a4ed6d00.jpg)

7) Disconnect the engine coolant outlet hose from the CVTF cooler (with warmer feature).

![](images/27f026b8a3369cfc57d4ab40762bc2859c4a904fa8da2104a272c74cf0c91aaa.jpg)

8) Remove the nut which secures the EGR cooler to the cylinder block RH.

![](images/5aa28055ee06f3560ef1b9a53cb6008ecb6213736eb2b66030e9f3e3c91951c3.jpg)

EC(H4DOTC)-35

9) Disconnect the water hose from the water pipe RH.

![](images/776cabf5f9edf932e18e6853229f562c4b20012f7be778d4a0efbb639ee8acd8.jpg)

10) Lower the vehicle.
11) Disconnect the engine coolant inlet hose from the EGR cooler.

![](images/fea39ab12241dbddba5adcd67fe55951ca340d584a9049f9c6cecc3382b8d0f3.jpg)

12) Remove the bolts which secure the EGR cooler to the EGR control valve and cylinder head RH, and remove the EGR cooler.

![](images/6cb35d79adb1bf0c5cde3b607e3fde5b6877382f60c14c43c36ebc0d480da0d5.jpg)

13) Remove the gasket (A) from the stud bolt, and remove the stud bolt from the cylinder head RH.

EC(H4DOTC)-37

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the stud bolt to the cylinder head RH, and set the gasket (A) to the stud bolt. NOTE:
Use a new stud bolt and gasket.

Tightening torque: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)

![](images/e5e32e656af1b40a53ccf1e4105c589d13685c6468e7ddded47f11cc1ad6e987.jpg)

2) Set the EGR cooler to the EGR control valve and cylinder head RH, and install the bolts which secure the EGR cooler to the EGR control valve and cylinder head RH.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: T1: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb) T2: 19 N·m (1.9 kgf-m, 14.0 ft-lb)

![](images/5554ba147e68231fdcb5f8cf79f8f563a2ca02775f69191692f2ce3b6198687d.jpg)

### EC(H4DOTC)-38

3) Connect the engine coolant inlet hose to the EGR cooler.

![](images/a0f847b5dcb50964be5651dc235e0239630ab02d180ac2e8015f0984cf2c1957.jpg)

4) Lift up the vehicle.
5) Connect the water hose to the water pipe RH.

![](images/ba352e6a5c7d1390367fd52f9749aac7b6b0a6404599746254a0708a9a375c8b.jpg)

6) Install the EGR cooler to the cylinder block RH. (1) Tighten the nuts which secure the EGR cooler to the cylinder block RH in numerical order as shown in the figure.

Tightening torque: 9 N·m (0.9 kgf-m, 6.6 ft-lb)

![](images/b8a9f530aea465891c553e2485580c635ffae4b55ae44dccb847070fbc8e88e8.jpg)

(2) Retighten the nut shown in the figure.

Tightening torque: 9 N·m (0.9 kgf-m, 6.6 ft-lb)

![](images/71b5d9f196e07a94df2b2b314239bc2254a56a7c9f773d4b47b3e1bd4c2381c8.jpg)

7) Connect the engine coolant outlet hose to the CVTF cooler (with warmer feature).

![](images/a61e87d7e1d11f68771eea33ec803df3274a2d9c460704f9d1957ca008159aa5.jpg)

8) Lower the vehicle.
9) Install the clip which secures the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold.
10) Install the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-37, INSTALLATION, Intercooler.>
11) Connect the battery ground terminal.
12) Fill engine coolant. <Ref. to CO(H4DOTC)-14, FILLING OF ENGINE COOLANT, REPLACEMENT, En
gine Coolant.>
13) Install the collector cover.

![](images/517fe12bf9ed8edfc9523f6f29010fbf58224c0af48f0225cfec60f52f2a0fee.jpg)

### C: DISASSEMBLY

Remove the water hose from EGR cooler.

![](images/5415a6b1ba5bacc541f2895f89a46984cbd7b4922e395e627549303430ec103e.jpg)

1) Check that the EGR cooler has no deformation, cracks or other damages.

### A: SPECIFICATION

The leak check valve assembly is a non-disassembled part. Do not remove the drain filter from the leak check valve assembly. Refer to “Leak Check Valve Assembly” for removal and installation procedures. <Ref. to EC(H4DOTC)-46, REMOVAL, Leak Check Valve Assembly.> <Ref. to EC(H4DOTC)-52, INSTALLATION, Leak Check Valve Assembly.>

EC(H4DOTC)-45

### A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
2) Lift up the vehicle.
3) Remove the rear exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-45, REMOVAL, Rear Exhaust Pipe.>
4) Remove the propeller shaft. <Ref. to DS-11, REMOVAL, Propeller Shaft.>
5) Support the rear differential with the transmission jack.
6) Remove the self-locking nuts which hold the rear differential to the rear sub frame assembly.

![](images/67c414d201efd360dae6e7935f3b3faf361f78ac313bc139a8b3191002405b52.jpg)

7) Remove the rear differential member from the rear sub frame assembly and the rear differential.

![](images/1226036c2cba8053980a9bca518957afd506876006ff94717a089da84a52744d.jpg)

8) Lower the transmission jack gradually until the rear differential is at the position shown in the figure. NOTE:

• When pulling out the stud bolt from the bushing portion of the rear sub frame assembly, adjust the angle and location of transmission jack and jack stand.

![](images/7b91fca3fabd0bb9aa8c07f4d2f5a7de219b51cdbb36ea898d9de5ee830e6290.jpg)

Do not lower the rear differential excessively. Doing so may add extra load to the drive shaft or cause the falling-off of the drive shaft.

![](images/4f4e623d41c3dc956f03c9204a7a135c89a7d6ca5016bfe978ffd8fc0c3152ef.jpg)

### EC(H4DOTC)-47

9) Disconnect the drain tube from the canister. NOTE: Disconnect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/95a7c58922fcce44626c6ba75a7eb92ea502b112686b039413e158658735fa69.jpg)

![](images/aa605bf07c2ed8b493ccd813a365a53218bc95d060c23ce12066b29fe55b0798.jpg)
10) Disconnect the fuel filler hose (A) and evaporation hose (B).

EC(H4DOTC)-49

11) Disconnect the drain tube from the drain pipe of the fuel filler pipe assembly. NOTE:
Disconnect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/4928345e6ccf74b459a4b842bcf23bf853c2e9136efef4d0f5ad284b8fb22cf8.jpg)

12) Disconnect the connector from the leak check valve assembly.

![](images/a7a0ec84e451a9ade19f7a72e7908a413d437009213a2c1092e5cddcfcba5138.jpg)

13) Remove the bolt and clip (A) which secure the leak check valve assembly to the vehicle, and remove the leak check valve assembly.

![](images/61d70a2847342bbf4eab2446c6710fcdd6aee9a6b2529e746db5fa26eea5a9ce.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the leak check valve assembly to the vehicle with the bolt and clip (A).

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/283ac53646b8108027dc7a8ddc0ee59ffb75edaca207861105f526811ab48e76.jpg)

2) Connect the connector to the leak check valve assembly.

![](images/a91f96eb208c18f347661e4af0d0327dbccb5c1ab765da9dd751306df457bedf.jpg)

3) Connect the drain tube to the drain pipe of the fuel filler pipe assembly.

CAUTION:

• Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. If necessary, clean the seal surface
of the pipe. Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

NOTE: Connect

![](images/011f67cf4e78fdcfe7d7dd50b85253975e8920c10cfca41c022fa7b46c2e8603.jpg)

4) Securely insert the fuel filler hose (A) and evaporation hose (B) until the hose end contacts the spool, then attach the clamp and clip as shown in the figure.

Tightening torque: 2.5 N·m (0.3 kgf-m, 1.8 ft-lb)

![](images/e6c2f14e472025a418fc233cef8a387710d88728f7b35543653a9c7d26c8b162.jpg)

(1) Hose (3) Spool (4) Pipe (2) Clamp and clip

5) Connect the drain tube to the canister.

CAUTION:

• Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. If necessary, clean the seal surface
of the pipe. Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

NOTE: Connect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/52968ecd6b89ab83080b07fb6d07c58116fbe4d43948683745b84ff878a8b1e2.jpg)

6) Lift up the transmission jack gradually, and set the rear differential to the rear sub frame assembly.

NOTE:

When inserting the stud bolt into the bushing portion of the rear sub frame assembly, adjust the angle and location of transmission jack and jack stand.

![](images/deb9838b9063f273fcc9e0038356fbbb842d992361a37ba7140f1b06bf2e6630.jpg)

7) Temporarily tighten the self-locking nuts which hold the rear differential to the rear sub frame assembly. NOTE:
Use a new self-locking nut.

![](images/71567fb7d38b3714b23a23ff1b8974c0e4951ef7e1118f55b5c842d449219340.jpg)

8) Set the rear differential member to the rear sub frame assembly and rear differential, and temporarily tighten the self-lock nuts which secure the rear differential member to the rear sub frame assembly and rear differential.

NOTE: Use a new self-locking nut.

![](images/5e986348e2443b4aa22e6ece7fc7958a214c50f8952c23eab146cd352971966e.jpg)

9) Remove the transmission jack from the rear differential.
10) Tighten the self-locking nuts which secure the rear differential member to the rear sub frame assembly and rear differential.

Tightening torque: T1: 50 N·m (5.1 kgf-m, 36.9 ft-lb) T2: 110 N·m (11.2 kgf-m, 81.1 ft-lb)

![](images/7f35a9633e1e4113f118ef98baeac8bfed59059b6f11fd550c9ceff6ad832ea8.jpg)

11) Tighten the self-locking nuts which secure the rear differential to the rear sub frame assembly.

Tightening torque: 70 N·m (7.1 kgf-m, 51.6 ft-lb)

![](images/0147aeef6729229ffff9952f206457df2bc37613f51228c1cfd327da55a5f971.jpg)

12) Install the propeller shaft. <Ref. to DS-13, INSTALLATION, Propeller Shaft.>

### B: INSTALLATION

13) Install the rear exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-46, INSTALLATION, Rear Exhaust Pipe.>
14) Lower the vehicle.
15) Connect the battery ground terminal.

### C: DISASSEMBLY

1) Disconnect the drain tube from the leak check valve assembly. NOTE: Disconnect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/25657e5b417681007c294c83579d3ab90bd6eb3a3760acb288d9113d08fe823e.jpg)

2) Remove the bracket from the leak check valve assembly.

![](images/aa62ec1eb363e79fc5539fee3fff34ccc9e0308505fb0416b3feb5ba1e89bd23.jpg)

### D: ASSEMBLY

1) Install the bracket to the leak check valve assembly.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/1f2494d93bc925a52fee73a0936bab05edf528111a5ae8719ece238fee0ed190.jpg)

2) Install the drain tube to the leak check valve assembly.

CAUTION:

• Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. If necessary, clean the seal surface
of the pipe. Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

NOTE: Connect the quick connector as shown in the figure.

![](images/08c1d72ce458684f250992326c5160d9af8357e7694fdec19675eeb2655fb6f7.jpg)

### 1. CHECK SWITCHING VALVE

1) Check the resistance between switching valve terminals.

![](images/924be6f9c2c446a93eef4315e0f6a150dfc356e44ac3bcc325340b880ca3245b.jpg)

EC-02813

![](images/0c5109b34beaed79839cb29b6782116a44979e44f013da63968615da7c4f00c7.jpg)

2) Check that air is discharged from (B) when air is blown into (A).

![](images/b9b74722f6678ccca83d0891a911cfe6cc8ac0a40586920d88e7ce680dd1cd5c.jpg)

EC-03403

### Leak Check Valve Assembly

3) Connect the battery positive terminal to the terminal No. 5 and the battery negative terminal to the terminal No. 1. Check that air does not come out from (B) when air is blown into (A).

![](images/8a1bbe41808e49f0df78275052fa269cf95eb6dca60859aa461a49bf8c0974ed.jpg)

### 2. CHECK VACUUM PUMP

1) Connect the battery positive terminal to terminal No. 3 and the battery ground terminal to terminal No. 4, and inspect the vacuum pump operation.

CAUTION: Do not operate the vacuum pump for 5 minutes or more.

![](images/9db4ffdc26cd718eaaf4a4005c4063f4c2b8aee4be87b32f5b2c7b70601c0103.jpg)

### 3. CHECK PRESSURE SENSOR

1) Connect dry-cell battery positive terminal to terminal No. 6 and dry-cell battery ground terminal to terminal No. 8, circuit tester positive terminal to terminal No. 7 and the circuit tester negative terminal to terminal No. 8.

NOTE:

Use new dry-cell batteries. Using circuit tester, check the voltage of a single dry-cell battery is 1.6 V or more. And also check the voltage of three batteries in series is between 4.8 V and 5.2 V.

![](images/c2b12fa7fdd654b026277f7d7b031f73c85cd705d29af12ff171650596100807.jpg)

2) Check the voltage at a normal atmospheric pressure.

NOTE:

The atmospheric pressure at higher altitude is lower than normal. Therefore, the voltage is lower than the standard value.

![](images/5559ff006ad3114debf4169e008bf377d92997015ba50227b6c5596d7d7db112.jpg)

3) Connect the battery positive terminal to terminal No. 3 and the battery ground terminal to terminal No. 4, and check that there is a voltage drop from the voltage measured in step 2) when the vacuum pump is operated.

![](images/b2691860ed8d3d2be3a7d66dc8b0c596da6e2168096f335b54af5455a5a56726.jpg)
EC(H4DOTC)-64

### 4. OTHER INSPECTIONS

1) Check that the leak check valve assembly has no deformation, cracks or other damages.
2) Check that the tube or hose have no cracks, damage or loose part.

EC(H4DOTC)-65

### 13.PCV Pipe

A: REMOVAL

CAUTION:

Do not remove except when the PCV pipe is broken.

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/8c60ab45b779bd393bc53ef719d39ee434cad4694dc02f9a4b73aa282bf876f5.jpg)

2) Collect the refrigerant from A/C system. <Ref. to AC-26, Refrigerant Recovery Procedure.>
3) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
4) Disconnect the PCV pipe from the intake duct No. 1, and remove the clip (A) from the PCV pipe.

![](images/b2d3a09cfc8cf478b84600e9ea8df2cb908207ea6ff1505fa332c05479f4fcd8.jpg)

5) Remove the clip securing the PCV pipe to the intake manifold.

![](images/4bfee652885a5296e2a060a243bbbb63c57880243a0ca763030f6d1704ae7507.jpg)

6) Remove the A/C compressor. <Ref. to AC-52, REMOVAL, Compressor.>
7) Remove the PCV pipe from the PCV connector.

![](images/85a25ea14fe4cd33e9a9295611c3553acf4920d7b4582b27543e395b348a07b1.jpg)

### 14.PCV Connector

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/6efe57f87c14418fb837fea04d8aba362da3640f5b05eef8273b06e48f5e6910.jpg)

2) Collect the refrigerant from A/C system. <Ref. to AC-26, Refrigerant Recovery Procedure.>
3) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
4) Drain engine coolant. <Ref. to CO(H4DOTC)-13, DRAINING OF ENGINE COOLANT, REPLACEMENT, Engine Coolant.>
5) Remove the A/C compressor. <Ref. to AC-52, REMOVAL, Compressor.>
6) Disconnect the preheater hose and PCV pipe from the PCV connector, and remove the PCV connector from the cylinder block LH.

![](images/559f16564d529aadaa7bc5f37ffe1d519b2bc84c7fe3b0365cf9d3e033afda04.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

Install in the reverse order of removal. NOTE:
Use new O-rings.
Tightening torque: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)
C: INSPECTION
Check that the PCV connector has no deformation, cracks or other damages.

### 15.PCV Hose

A: REMOVAL

CAUTION:

Do not remove except when the PCV hose is broken.

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/ff004f5383ad82167e8a4f2b83f99948ffe30348a078414803e14966c4a64bd8.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Remove the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-35, REMOVAL, Intercooler.>
4) Remove the clip securing the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold, and move the brake booster vacuum hose at the locations that do not interfere operation.

![](images/8783e94d22f592e6452f80e7e09cd7c486a0bba0056978119cf55a59841cba3b.jpg)

5) Disconnect the PCV hose A from the intake manifold, and remove the PCV hose A from the PCV valve.

![](images/769a35848a53ca82746c229228cf8cccfba62599a2a099ba34256e729643f06b.jpg)

### 16.PCV Hose Assembly

A: REMOVAL

CAUTION: Do not remove except when the PCV hose assembly is broken.

1) Remove the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.> 2) Disconnect the PCV hose assembly from the chain cover, and remove the PCV hose assembly from the oil catch tank.

NOTE:

To disconnect the PCV hose assembly, fit the cut outs of the ST with the protrusions on the clamp as shown in the figure, squeeze the ST's handles together and unlock the clamp.
ST 18353AA000 CLAMP PLIERS

![](images/7706e6f55da75a67d33a0795e3f47c490dc8a3946d87f6686cc18329242f616d.jpg)

EC(H4DOTC)-72

### B: INSTALLATION

Install in the reverse order of removal.

NOTE:
Use a new clamp. To connect the PCV hose assembly, fit the cut outs of the ST with the protrusions on the clamp as shown in the figure, squeeze the ST's handles together and lock the clamp.
ST 18353AA000 CLAMP PLIERS

![](images/605d04ef4c18eba3ceebe21b61b1c82533f66ea5efaaf2df0306eec916480e75.jpg)

### 17.PCV Valve

A: REMOVAL

CAUTION:

Do not remove unless the PCV valve is broken.

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/448db51fe64d2140d15b47fccc1581f5488ba16f31adaed8f031534ec252a21b.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Remove the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-35, REMOVAL, Intercooler.>
4) Remove the clip securing the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold, and move the brake booster vacuum hose at the locations that do not interfere operation.

![](images/a25264db4a3e654d479f7fb49e808023f833abc7fa53014da0b07afe52cb2077.jpg)

5) Disconnect the PCV hose from the PCV valve.

![](images/075a01e9b93199ff524956055f6db136f5a45c79dda4882275d520788f88cb4f.jpg)

6) Remove the PCV valve from the cylinder block RH.

![](images/40d15c7d4912fd9ef5ee74bf280906cc1506e79b8a9da506c00fc34f595ed572.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

Install in the reverse order of removal.

NOTE: Apply liquid gasket to the bolt threads of PCV valve.

Liquid gasket: THREE BOND 1324 (Part No. 004403042) or equivalent

Tightening torque: 23 N·m (2.3 kgf-m, 17.0 ft-lb)

EC(H4DOTC)-75

### C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the PCV valve has no deformation, cracks or other damages.
2) Check that air is discharged from (B) when air is blown into (A).

![](images/524f5e22e26324ed54c547aabd4953575574c6f85dd8b95653ab1a429dfa3344.jpg)

EC-02816

3) Check that air does not come out from (B) when air is blown into (A).

![](images/3116eea9db887b3d65f730517e4d7fa8d936977775bcbda5a6c94fd2b2cea167.jpg)

EC-02817

### B: CAUTION

Prior to starting work, pay special attention to the following:

1. Always wear work clothes, a safety cap, protective shoes. Additionally, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary. 2. Protect the vehicle using a seat cover, fender cover, etc. 3. Prepare the service tools, clean cloth, containers to catch grease and oil, etc. • Vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts. When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and replacement. • Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery. • Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle. • Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation, disassembly or assembly. • Keep the removed parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt. • All removed parts, if to be reused, should be reinstalled in the original positions with attention to the correct directions, etc. • Bolts, nuts and washers should be replaced with new parts as required. • Be sure to tighten the fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

### A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the clip (A) from the air cleaner case (rear).

![](images/11cfd1a83c1840d496acb44d941aaba2a584fb6b49e2a22ad0c7a2aedd857527.jpg)

2) Open the air cleaner case, and remove the air cleaner element.

![](images/5f8cd1cfe410a1e9039b4cc4edb7fc178caf3312afebb1db83c41878a622fa97.jpg)

IN(H4DOTC)-7

### B: INSTALLATION

Install in the reverse order of removal.

NOTE:

• Be sure to use SUBARU genuine air cleaner element depending on the engine type when replacing the air cleaner elements. Using other air cleaner elem ent may affect the engine performance. • Check that there are no foreign objects in the air cleaner case. • If the protrusion of the air cleaner case (rear) is removed when removing the air cleaner element, align the protrusion of the air cleaner case (rear) to the hole on the air cleaner case (front) to install.

![](images/3e1f7e0bac164282f514a0876a9d34f691a6d86bcd9fbe49d74867ef2f13f4be.jpg)

### C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the air cleaner element has no deformation, cracks or other damages.
2) Check the air cleaner element for excessive dirt.

### A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.

2) Remove the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.> 3) Remove the engine control module (ECM). <Ref. to FU(H4DOTC)-134, REMOVAL, Engine Control Module (ECM).> 4) Remove the clips (2 places) which secure the front mud guard RH to the vehicle.

![](images/619e775a617b5202f853d930b7e6a9ec59ab7fec8ada3515d49d5131da22560e.jpg)

5) Turn over the front mud guard RH, and loosen the clamp which secures the air intake boot to the air cleaner case (rear).

![](images/7cbdea752c7d593074bc104e90555c33f6648177396286cc5d3796c822f145d8.jpg)

IN(H4DOTC)-9

6) Disconnect the connector (A) from the mass air flow and intake air temperature sensor, and remove the clip (B) from the air cleaner case (rear).

![](images/b95e039bdea835bfc34cde4d9fb3537b1984a677afc07c7b18fe055e6d87a043.jpg)

7) Remove the air cleaner case (rear) and air cleaner element.
8) Remove bolts (A) and nuts (B) which secure the air cleaner case (front) to the body and air cleaner case bracket, and remove the air cleaner case (front).

![](images/ebd3f0a3ac7dd9789e09f531b38b88dea9b8fc3a8fe1d0f3627063d07e3a70a2.jpg)

IN(H4DOTC)-10

9) Remove the air cleaner case bracket from the vehicle.

![](images/f00ca85b245d0dc1ad52065339c356e1f4fec5872015b433728c1ff836e8eedd.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the air cleaner case bracket to the vehicle.

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/dfbefe165672066af361093bbad2dc050fad685fd22b7029df92858b15f4759f.jpg)

2) Install the bolt (A) and nut (B) which secure the air cleaner case (front) to the vehicle and to the air cleaner case bracket.

Tightening torque: Bolt (A) 6 N·m (0.6 kgf-m, 4.4 ft-lb) Nut (B) 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/7761478ad08a82ffdf44d787bfe816486dd52ac2b51ea0110c80338a1ec3ce1a.jpg)

3) Set the air cleaner element to the air cleaner case (front), and install the air cleaner case (rear).

When installing the air cleaner case (rear), align the protrusion of the air cleaner case (rear) to the hole on the air cleaner case (front) to install.

![](images/4bbca90aa9668795cc305b92e929b8f5ba4825a8e4ebc3652811565ca364c363.jpg)

4) Install the clip (B) to the air cleaner case (rear), and connect the connector (A) to the mass air flow and intake air temperature sensor.

![](images/d5e8c22abe9a293ad5175a9dec8683f7376982a42daafebe335b7a6a326e9a22.jpg)

5) Tighten the clamp which secures the air intake boot to the air cleaner case (rear).

Tightening torque: 2.5 N·m (0.3 kgf-m, 1.8 ft-lb)

![](images/8d6f1aee756352c909ffbd6b32869866564378c60c6d0251ddc6f273ba4f4bde.jpg)

6) Set the front mud guard RH to the vehicle, and install the clips which secure the front mud guard RH.

![](images/3d9451839fcf948b53a9a84ba58ec2953e92ed7eed2c70fcdc0d3fece33ab178.jpg)

7) Install the engine control module (ECM). <Ref. to FU(H4DOTC)-136, INSTALLATION, Engine Control Module (ECM).>
8) Install the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Duct.>
9) Connect the battery ground terminal.

### A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.

IN-03366

(g) Protrusion portion

### A: REMOVAL

### 1. INTAKE DUCT NO. 1

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
2) Remove the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.>
3) Disconnect the vacuum hose from vacuum pipe.
4) Lift up the vehicle.
5) Remove the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.>
6) Disconnect the connector from the wastegate control solenoid valve.

![](images/30ab8d2bbf9b52dccefbed9f7806d7284b4c80e3f8954721c56cad138ce530d4.jpg)

![](images/636d9225c233c2c27ee45bea2e5a2f1460757c58b0b10ead642bd561d90b106b.jpg)

7) Disconnect the PCV pipe (A) from the intake duct No. 1, and disconnect the vacuum control hose (B) from the wastegate control solenoid valve.

![](images/f4b0998f748f5345d2f75d5ce42a8a0b980e4e6727f2868d1961e85c53815976.jpg)

8) Remove the air intake boot from the intake duct No. 1, and disengage the clip which secures the air bypass valve to the intake duct No. 1.

![](images/7a71bebdda21dbfeac8625bfb11d11deb7b933220925d20e155c367291924755.jpg)

9) Remove the bolts which secure the intake duct No. 1 to the turbocharger, and remove the intake duct No. 1.

![](images/c48b718b651ad507d70e86ab7b57378ff763dbe359e71aeb9ac5e19974f7ef9f.jpg)

### 2. INTAKE DUCT NO. 2

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/32ce2e2be245f6977f68fe8ab2678f369b9703d6c9eb8975833b9927df5bfb91.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Remove the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.>
4) Remove the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-35, REMOVAL, Intercooler.>
5) Remove the radiator sub fan and fan motor assembly. <Ref. to CO(H4DOTC)-55, REMOVAL, Radiator
Sub Fan and Fan Motor.>
6) Lift up the vehicle.
7) Remove the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.>

8) Disconnect the PCV pipe (A) and vacuum hose (B) from the intake duct No. 1, and disconnect the vacuum hose (C) from the air by-pass valve.

![](images/6126aea7adc17621d00ab63fe5741be399f93195d272aeb534b2744aeca0798a.jpg)

10) Lower the vehicle.

11) Remove the bolts which secure the intake duct No. 2 to the turbocharger.

![](images/be51022e0c1b7a289e253bccf8f0febc5601c893d9f8c169e6b08528d74ce519.jpg)

12) Pull out the air by-pass valve from the intake duct No. 1, and remove the intake duct No. 2 from the intake manifold.

![](images/ac5815f83bdb3626cbf1d0aef5816b13e056f09e1532b38cfecb679f96e6591b.jpg)

### 3. INTAKE DUCT NO. 3

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/ade8426a7ddc629ac5f57ae581c051d309cc4f251345456e72aab1687248cd5d.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Remove the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-35, REMOVAL, Intercooler.>
4) Remove the clip securing the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold, and move the brake booster vacuum hose at the locations that do not interfere operation.

![](images/98abde53b8ff29d1d69f73e561a82d8a4c2bef2a146d01eb2d98f87d7ba93f2a.jpg)

### 1. INTAKE DUCT NO. 1

1) Install the intake duct No. 1 to the turbocharger.

NOTE:

Use new O-rings.
Be careful not to pinch the O-ring.
Check that the air by-pass valve is firmly inserted into the intake duct No. 1.

Tightening torque: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)

![](images/9287c52aa710ec58da1f9c3240869d47133864977624a1305243c34cd97af3e1.jpg)

2) Engage the clip which secures the air by-pass valve to the intake duct No. 1, and install the air intake boot to the intake duct No. 1.

![](images/c27a25a4ae52d2eb8fda182693ce2128e0c40a7e62442af8782714054f6915f7.jpg)

3) Connect the PCV pipe (A) to the intake duct No. 1, and connect the vacuum control hose (B) to the wastegate control solenoid valve.

![](images/f3e1b3e5d3f2b0c49890b634535c0e683af1caaff067f98eaa4b72aab2af1bcf.jpg)

### IN(H4DOTC)-27

4) Connect the connector to the wastegate control solenoid valve.

![](images/94727b197c88c102ae36d9e661cc799ba73c734c3d754b01167aa3154118e747.jpg)

5) Install the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, INSTALLATION, Front Under Cover.>
6) Lower the vehicle.
7) Connect the vacuum hose to the vacuum pipe.
8) Install the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Duct.>
9) Connect the battery ground terminal.
10) Install the collector cover.

![](images/86d4c706c64690e80c58b65bb1098a623b5656f98bab63690af07f7e3c6b8379.jpg)

### 2. INTAKE DUCT NO. 2

1) Set the air by-pass valve to the intake duct No. 1, and install the intake duct No. 2 to the intake manifold.

![](images/a902f71941b5e644e55739df9edeaed8fda0ec5310750a41bf0925907ca5b4d9.jpg)

2) Install the bolt which secure the intake duct No. 2 to the turbocharger.

NOTE:

Use new O-rings.
Be careful not to pinch the O-ring.
Check that the air by-pass valve is firmly inserted into the intake duct No. 1.

Tightening torque: 16 N·m (1.6 kgf-m, 1.8 ft-lb)

![](images/a6012aebb804c77f22a39ad6168d89072113581f2bdbcef47935e4ecd2342a74.jpg)

3) Lift up the vehicle.

4) Engage the clip which secures the air by-pass valve to the intake duct No. 1.

![](images/640d2985e7d33c6239e0e3f98276ebe048ce457f14d13c3426732d236f1f2244.jpg)

5) Connect the PCV pipe (A) and vacuum hose (B) to the intake duct No. 1, and connect the vacuum hose (C) to the air by-pass valve.

![](images/cd002c66d82bbf6f678e2055aa22457a047a295a6ac3918cd04e89f46dac798a.jpg)

6) Install the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, INSTALLATION, Front Under Cover.>
7) Lower the vehicle.
8) Install the radiator sub fan and fan motor assembly. <Ref. to CO(H4DOTC)-55, INSTALLATION, Radiator
Sub Fan and Fan Motor.>
9) Install the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-37, INSTALLATION, Intercooler.>
10) Install the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Duct.>
11) Connect the battery ground terminal.
12) Install the collector cover.

### 3. INTAKE DUCT NO. 3

1) Align the triangle mark (A) on the intake duct No. 3 to the rib (B) on the throttle body, and install the intake duct No. 3 to the throttle body.

NOTE:

Use a new insulator.
• Apply a thin coat of SUBARU PS fluid (K0515YA000) or liquid paraffin to the inner periphery of the insu
lator. When inserting the intake duct No. 3 to the throttle body, be careful that the insulator is not turned over.

### Tightening torque: 3 N·m (0.3 kgf-m, 2.2 ft-lb)

![](images/9573c7929e4289cef169e054bad3bcb6eec558d4dd2e3e1c2a9f0408d1e1a50a.jpg)

2) Install the clip which secures the brake booster vacuum hose to the intake manifold.

![](images/35a56a830ab4a567bb2795fcc0a2394f260c18545e8f89fa4bc3e67ecf2b9484.jpg)

3) Install the intercooler. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-37, INSTALLATION, Intercooler.>
4) Connect the battery ground terminal.
5) Install the collector cover.

Remove the vacuum hose and wastegate control solenoid valve from the intake duct.

1) Check that the intake duct has no deformation, cracks or other damages.

### A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the collector cover.

![](images/f7ceae6448902aaa4cf59c44c32bb7ce471a2cce43b8ef186805f4137a79e59d.jpg)

2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery. 3) While pressing the section (A) shown in the figure, move the lock lever (B) in the direction of the arrow to disconnect the connectors from the ECM in numerical order as shown in the figure.

![](images/f925f25e363b19cdc67e36cfd52a17250ce8da3c5bfcd32f94f0b23dcbe3dfde.jpg)

4) Loosen the clamp (A) which holds the intake duct to intercooler.

### IN(H4DOTC)-35

5) Remove the bolts which secure the intercooler to the intercooler stay, and remove the intercooler.

![](images/64663be28cc06d369996ff07085a0d4a93f129ef610b5cc6af16846f3474765e.jpg)

6) Remove the brake booster vacuum hose from the clip (A).
7) Remove the intercooler stay RH from the engine hanger stay, and remove the intercooler stay LH from the intake manifold.

![](images/cdf82018a09d12727fdc23b62abdcfa1717061f3be22bff290183e0db65d4887.jpg)

8) Remove the insulator and clamp from intake duct.

![](images/2d1b00f9a8d9ca818f4b27a082c0b3c3b01ba7ec5d0d287285ba7523b2fcf546.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the insulator and clamp to the intake duct.

NOTE:

Use a new insulator. Apply a thin coat of SUBARU PS fluid (K0515YA000) or liquid paraffin to the inner periphery of the insulator.

![](images/868c14e95f85a348e72a9b40a811143409c913daf5d3de7e8ed4448cd3b1fa43.jpg)

### IN(H4DOTC)-37

2) Install the intercooler stay RH to the engine hanger stay.

Tightening torque: 16 N·m (1.6 kgf-m, 11.8 ft-lb)

![](images/7a84b224b6c400f225b73e6d921d956b0854e1a71b8d9c3680144423280ebc9d.jpg)

3) Temporarily tighten the intercooler stay LH to the intake manifold.
4) Install the brake booster vacuum hose to the clip (A).

![](images/02ebddf7e26b701413d57810effce60be9215e982afa28905438ed0cf3a3c2ae.jpg)

5) Insert the intercooler into the intake duct No. 2, and temporarily tighten the clamp which secures the intake duct No. 2 to the intercooler.

NOTE: When inserting the intercooler into the intake duct No. 2, be careful that the insulator is not turned over.

![](images/f1c5432b207f2a2a57b2018e4f9233d872ab2f5dab154252bb5c1ca23d73af0f.jpg)

6) Insert the intercooler into the intake duct No. 3, and tighten the clamp which secures the intake duct to the intercooler.

NOTE: When inserting the intercooler into the intake duct No. 3, be careful that the insulator is not turned over.

Tightening torque: 3 N·m (0.3 kgf-m, 2.2 ft-lb)

![](images/750e4e7fa5d9b8a88ce93b0fa6fc97a3de3d00f19e65c6e207095c9219c6de2c.jpg)

7) Install the bolts which secure the intercooler to the intercooler stay, and tighten the bolt which secures the intercooler stay LH to the intake manifold.

Tightening torque: 16 N·m (1.6 kgf-m, 11.8 ft-lb)

![](images/0d9671498f884349377af2c7fb8af32e084336936d8d17895ce6067645d9fc80.jpg)

8) Move the lock lever in the direction of the arrow, and connect the connector to the ECM in numerical order as shown in the figure.

![](images/14e64046ae56370caffed097e50e599b294d3badc08833c6631a8fab5d43cbde.jpg)

9) Connect the battery ground terminal.
10) Install the collector cover.

### A: REMOVAL

Remove the turbo charger and front exhaust pipe as a unit. Refer to “Front Exhaust Pipe” for the removal procedure. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-7, REMOVAL, Front Exhaust Pipe.> <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-24, DISASSEMBLY, Front Exhaust Pipe.>

### B: INSTALLATION

Refer to “Front Exhaust Pipe” for the installation procedure. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-15, INSTALLATION, Front Exhaust Pipe.> <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-27, ASSEMBLY, Front Exhaust Pipe.>

### C: DISASSEMBLY

1) Remove the union screw pipe assembly from the turbocharger.

![](images/6dd89eb19ace7ab8659b4075a29203047e082d7f363f2a5ece17a73b8c34a27a.jpg)

IN-03251

2) Remove the turbocharger pipe from the turbocharger.

![](images/d68f2fefefb3fdfb85fd8b4b5def8b2456e9b3c56c19772e9cea699a5c9b1388.jpg)

3) Remove the air control hose from the turbocharger.

![](images/f1d488164326d86f7f50278171a4772373a46a939fd15515402ef444633331bb.jpg)

4) Remove the stud bolt from the turbocharger.

![](images/56ecba20cd7fdf7f46d3b2a9e5cd316628d3838ce9f747cc030b81161057aafe.jpg)

IN(H4DOTC)-42

5) Remove the exhaust stay from the turbocharger.

![](images/cf3749af74a5728453e6bf1d7480247f406c3a1d4fab587c63d65bea79e8ecf9.jpg)

IN-03255

### D: ASSEMBLY

1) Install the exhaust stay to the turbocharger.

Tightening torque: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)

![](images/4fe89492736f852f092131093abcee7a27f8dfd11d71deaf8c2ee9426f764cda.jpg)

IN-03255

2) Attach the stud bolts to the turbocharger.

Tightening torque: 14.7 N·m (1.5 kgf-m, 10.8 ft-lb)

![](images/929b3677f537ff61595b8d4d777ccced532eacb2ba7b63f66a95d2eea2ea6ba0.jpg)

3) Install the air control hose to the turbocharger.

![](images/586c1af61ca7bb832e046d0097535f7a4a6553074b65d3112e0d5e2d9f582f82.jpg)

IN-03253

### IN(H4DOTC)-44

4) Install the turbocharger pipe to the turbocharger.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: 31.5 N·m (3.2 kgf-m, 23.2 ft-lb)

![](images/9e6396b5006e5d30148a8f8f0bacc95247c524163fc78da5882465f35971fb66.jpg)

5) Install the union screw pipe assembly to the turbocharger. NOTE:
Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: T1: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb) T2: 16 N·m (1.6 kgf-m, 11.8 ft-lb)

![](images/6cc7a54b3dbe2a698a80f2e8a78764ef395ed4038cd09398f2f3d88179b81674.jpg)

IN-03256

### 1. WASTE GATE ACTUATOR

1) Remove the front exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-7, REMOVAL, Front Exhaust Pipe.>
2) Remove the exhaust cover.

![](images/094883ed7d1d95b34d14ec8136a31450d1c6a15d4b11f159eae63d96e789c07d.jpg)

3) Remove the vacuum control hose (B) from the waste gate actuator (A) of the turbocharger, and connect the Mighty Vac to the waste gate actuator (A).

![](images/9c8fab3250d6c445c7685fe5f57124dcd87638e68dca2ed3a1ba657eb6801c3b.jpg)

(A) Waste gate actuator (C) Control rod (D) Control rod stroke (B) Vacuum control hose

### IN(H4DOTC)-46

4) Pressurize slowly with the Mighty Vac, and check the pressure when the control rod stroke (D) becomes
10.15 mm (0.03940.0059 in). If it is not within the standard, replace the turbocharger assembly.

CAUTION:
Do not pressurize over 112.7 kPa (1.15 kgf/cm2, 16.34 psi) to prevent damaging the waste gate actuator.

Operating pressure (control rod stroke 10.15 mm (0.03940.0059 in)): Standard 84.0 — 88.0 kPa (0.86 — 0.90 kgf/cm2, 12.18 — 12.76 psi)

5) After inspection, install the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

Tightening torque: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)

### 2. OTHER INSPECTIONS

1) Check that the turbocharger and pipe have no deformation, cracks or other damages.
2) Check that the hose has no cracks, damage or loose part.
3) Check that there are no oil leakage or water leakage from the pipe attachment section.

### 9. Oil Catch Tank

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.>
2) Disconnect the PCV hose assembly from the oil catch tank.

NOTE:
To disconnect the PCV hose assembly, fit the cut outs of the ST with the protrusions on the clamp as shown in the figure, squeeze the ST's handles together and unlock the clamp.
ST 18353AA000 CLAMP PLIERS

![](images/514cf8f133f6f3ab392bafc138a9bc169c43f336c90d8fab112b7ae87c053866.jpg)

3) Lift up the vehicle.
4) Remove the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.>
5) Disconnect the turbocharger hose from the oil pipe, and drain the engine oil in the oil catch tank.

> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> Prepare the container for draining of engine oil.
>
> ![](images/058001fb87fe9c9e3b929c0c0eb27624ebb8d4510eb0a99cef9f9d4e2a64adba.jpg)
>
> 6) Remove bolts which secure the oil catch tank to the turbocharger and exhaust stay, and remove the oil catch tank.
>
> ![](images/897f3d4129e32e04ee7dd69172c46c320271dee9335d029ed4e8c1f78c6c9fbc.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the oil catch tank to the turbocharger and exhaust stay. (1) Set the oil catch tank to the turbocharger, and temporarily tighten the bolts which secure the oil catch tank to the turbocharger and exhaust stay.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

![](images/0273a419fa5389671267d3dc31c40f2d2ec5d23114919f05bc0dd55f7886b4a7.jpg)

(2) Tighten the bolts which secure the oil catch tank to the turbocharger and exhaust stay in numerical order as shown in the figure.

Tightening torque: T1: 6.4 N·m (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb) T2: 10.5 N·m (1.1 kgf-m, 7.7 ft-lb)

![](images/63e5ffa2df05c2f53089a355a4a66b304d6e846c62a13dbe9d21bc1df5a0afc5.jpg)

2) Connect the turbocharger hose to the oil pipe.

![](images/3d67ef3001a6e3ac02decf7d92f2a35f7d6b154a17ff2349c61a4be611e3dc96.jpg)

3) Install the under cover. <Ref. to EI-22, INSTALLATION, Front Under Cover.>
4) Lower the vehicle.

5) Connect the PCV hose assembly to the oil catch tank.

NOTE:

Use a new clamp. To connect the PCV hose assembly, fit the cut outs of the ST with the protrusions on the clamp as shown in the figure, squeeze the ST's handles together and lock the clamp. ST 18353AA000 CLAMP PLIERS

![](images/6d133567a5a3e9f4906447c54512dcc5fc9d407d88882a501fb3fa5f05796fd2.jpg)

6) Install the air intake duct (rear). <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-19, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Duct.> 7) Check the engine oil level and replenish the engine oil if necessary. <Ref. to LU(H4DO)-13, INSPECTION, Engine Oil.>

### C: DISASSEMBLY

Disconnect the turbo charger hose (A) from the oil catch tank, and remove the exhaust cover from the o catch tank.

![](images/407be4460a20cf48030cac60fc2cf7e64b45e7442235a4c669766ef9bd1d1fe3.jpg)

### E: INSPECTION

1) Check that the oil catch tank does not have deformation, cracks or damage.
2) Check that the PCV hose and turbocharger hose have no cracks, damage or loose part.

### 11.Air By-pass Valve

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the intake duct No. 1. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-20, INTAKE DUCT NO. 1, REMOVAL, Intake Duct.> 2) Disconnect the vacuum hose from the air by-pass valve, and remove the air by-pass valve from the intake duct No. 2.

![](images/5ee4f05f66e5c86c6819baa9895a4173e065cd776a6e17fe3aa66642a3dcd3eb.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

Install in the reverse order of removal.

Tightening torque: 3 N·m (0.3 kgf-m, 2.2 ft-lb) C: INSPECTION

### 1. AIR BY-PASS VALVE

1) Check that the air by-pass valve has no deformation, cracks or other damages.
2) Connect the Mighty Vac to the nipple (A) of the air by-pass valve.

![](images/b1363c1055be3441a646b8f39c8b494622e47971913437ae5ff9fd2189920d6c.jpg)

### Air By-pass Valve

3) Using the Mighty Vac, generate the vacuum pressure to –93.3 kPa (–0.95 kgf/cm2, –13.5 psi). Check that the Mighty Vac gauge needle holds 10 seconds without falling by –92.6 kPa (–0.94 kgf/cm2, –13.4 psi). 4) Set a dial gauge to the end of valve rod of the air by-pass valve.

![](images/bb870cb9836c69b5e38415e8161f81c9a697d10f3d0b7ea4795e6b423fe20cf0.jpg)

5) Using the Mighty Vac, generate the negative pressure, and check the pressure when dial gauge needle (valve stroke) shows 0.5 mm (0.02 in). If it is not within the standard, replace the air by-pass valve.

Opening pressure (valve stroke 0.5 mm (0.02 in)): Standard –13.3 — –21.3 kPa (–0.14 — –0.22 kgf/cm2, –1.93 — –3.09 psi)

### B: INSTALLATION

The resonator chamber and air cleaner case are integrated into one unit; therefore, refer to “Air Cleaner Case” for installation procedure. <Ref. to IN(H4DOTC)-11, INSTALLATION, Air Cleaner Case.>

### C: CAUTION

Prior to starting work, pay special attention to the following: 1. Always wear work clothes, a safety cap, protective shoes. Additionally, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary. 2. Protect the vehicle using a seat cover, fender cover, etc. 3. Prepare the service tools, clean cloth, containers to catch grease and oil, etc.
• Vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated
parts.
• When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and
replacement.
• Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery.
• Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle.
• Remove or install the engine in an area where chain hoists, lifting devices, etc. are available for ready use.
When lifting up the vehicle, make sure to support the vehicle at the jack-up points.
• Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation, disassembly or assembly.
• Keep the removed parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.
• All removed parts, if to be reused, should be reinstalled in the original positions with attention to the correct
directions, etc.
• Rotating parts and sliding parts such as piston, bearing and gear should be coated with oil when being as
sembled.
• Bolts, nuts and washers should be replaced with new parts as required. Be sure to tighten the fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

### A: INSPECTION

CAUTION:

After warming-up, engine becomes very hot. Be careful not to burn yourself during measurement.

1) After warming-up the engine, turn the ignition switch to OFF.
2) Make sure that the battery is fully charged.
3) Check the starter motor for satisfactory performance and operation.
4) Remove the fuse of fuel pump from main fuse box.
5) Start the engine and run it until it stalls.
6) After the engine stalls, crank it for five more seconds.
7) Turn the ignition switch to OFF.
8) Remove all spark plugs. <Ref. to IG(H4DOTC)-4, REMOVAL, Spark Plug.>
9) Install the compression gauge to the spark plug hole.

![](images/bf1aac51c7a93a5871623eb898c1afc8c6f1fa4af2ff85dbc88ca95be0c5086b.jpg)

NOTE: When using a screw-in type compression gauge, the screw should be less than 25 mm (0.98 in) long.

![](images/ad182f015a912f1d7e26a910985d73b871dfdd69798bc7944d14907348e5ede6.jpg)

### ME(H4DOTC)-21

10) Install the engine control module (ECM). <Ref. to FU(H4DOTC)-136, INSTALLATION, Engine Control Module (ECM).>

11) Install the battery. <Ref. to SC(H4DO)-63, INSTALLATION, Battery.>

12) Turn the ignition switch to ON.
13) Fully open the throttle valve.
14) Crank the engine by starter motor and read the value when the needle of the compression gauge becomes stable.

NOTE:

Perform at least two measurements per cylinder, and make sure that the values are correct.
If the compression pressure is out of standard, check or adjust the pistons, valves and cylinders.

Compression (fully open throttle): Standard 1,350 — 1,750 kPa (14 — 18 kgf/cm2, 196 — 254 psi) Difference between cylinders 100 kPa (1 kgf/cm2, 14 psi) or less

15) After inspection, install the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

NOTE:

When compression pressure is checked, the malfunction indicator light illuminates and DTC (P0087) may be stored in ECM. When the malfunction indicator light has illuminated, perform the Clear Memory Mode. <Ref. to EN(H4DOTC)(diag)-60, Clear Memory Mode.>

### A: INSPECTION

1) Before checking the idle speed, check the following item:

(1) Check the air cleaner element is free from clogging, ignition timing is correct, spark plugs are in good condition, and hoses are connected properly.
(2) Check the malfunction indicator light does not illuminate. 2) Warm up the engine.
3) Read the engine idle speed using Subaru Select Monitor. <Ref. to EN(H4DOTC)(diag)-37, DISPLAY CURRENT ENGINE DATA, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.>

NOTE:

• Idle speed cannot be adjusted manually, because the idle speed is automatically adjusted.
• If idle speed is out of standard, refer to the General Diagnosis Table under “Engine Control System”. <Ref.
to EN(H4DOTC)(diag)-2, Basic Diagnostic Procedure.> (1) Check the idle speed when no-loaded. (Headlight, blower fan, rear defroster, radiator fan, A/C and etc. are OFF)

Idle rpm (no load and select lever in “P” or “N” range): Standard 700100 rpm (2) Check the idle speed when loaded. (Turn the A/C switch to ON and operate the compressor for at least one minute before measurement.)

Idle speed (A/C ON and select lever in “P” or “N” range): Standard 700 — 83550 rpm

### A: INSPECTION

CAUTION:

After warming-up, engine becomes very hot. Be careful not to burn yourself at measurement.

1) Before checking the ignition timing, check the following item: (1) Check the air cleaner element is free from clogging, spark plugs are in good condition, and hoses are connected properly. (2) Check the malfunction indicator light does not illuminate.
2) Warm up the engine.
3) Read the ignition timing using Subaru Select Monitor. <Ref. to EN(H4DOTC)(diag)-37, DISPLAY CUR
RENT ENGINE DATA, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.>
NOTE:
If ignition timing is out of standard, check the ignition control system. Refer to “Engine Control System”. <Ref.
to EN(H4DOTC)(diag)-2, Basic Diagnostic Procedure.>

Ignition timing [BTDC/rpm]: Standard 10°10°/700

### A: INSPECTION

1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the co lector cover.

![](images/71593ef26cd5fc043578ab0a0fbc4ba8ab5e6af70271693585b489352b51c329.jpg)

2) Warm up the engine.
3) Disconnect the brake booster vacuum hose from the intake manifold.

![](images/f82c081a7889b48ba6d5b2e948eb0364748a01f5ca70e56f08942e687c8a7162.jpg)

4) Connect the vacuum gauge to the intake manifold.

![](images/5bbe89963d035f2b0ce501d108c38978ba0a173ce534cf429f5a10c5ac448d06.jpg)

5) Keep the engine at idle speed and read the vacuum gauge indication.

NOTE:

Condition of engine inside can be diagnosed by observing the behavior of the vacuum gauge needle as described in table below.

Intake manifold vacuum (at idling, A/C OFF): Standard –60.0 kPa (–450 mmHg, –17.72 inHg) or more

### A: INSPECTION

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
2) Remove the oil pressure switch. <Ref. to LU(H4DO)-42, REMOVAL, Oil Pressure Switch.>
3) Install the oil pressure gauge to the chain cover.
4) Connect the battery ground terminal.
5) Start the engine, and check the oil pressure.

![](images/ee84a2aa20682da8e5cf08e84b2df4d2a1f74bbcb5dc5594747ce4b6be867f8d.jpg)

NOTE:

• Standard value is based on an engine oil temperature of 80°C (176°F).
• If the oil pressure is out of specification, check oil pump, oil filter and lubrication line. <Ref. to LU(H4DO)- 105, INSPECTION, Engine Lubrication System Trouble in General.>
• If the oil pressure warning light is ON and oil pressure is within standard, check the oil pressure switch. <Ref. to LU(H4DO)-105, INSPECTION, Engine Lubrication System Trouble in General.>

Engine oil pressure: Standard 50 kPa (0.5 kgf/cm2, 7 psi) or more (at 600 rpm) 350 kPa (3.6 kgf/cm2, 51 psi) or more (at 6,000 rpm)

6) After inspection, install the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

### A: INSPECTION

Catch the fuel from the tubes using a container or cloth.

### Fuel Pressure

### 1. WHEN TIMING CHAIN ASSEMBLY IS NOT REMOVED

CAUTION:

When working on the vehicle, if engine oil is spilt onto the exhaust pipe, wipe it off with cloth to avoid emission of smoke or causing a fire.

NOTE:

• Inspection of cam clearance should be performed while engine is cold. If the engine is removed from vehicle, performing the step 1) is not necessary.
1) Remove the clip (A), lift the front of the collector cover in the direction of arrow, and then remove the col
lector cover.

![](images/b6bebaafe92ba1abe1b4e9d534061535b80dfbdfa2244c2767c31b30a02987b7.jpg)

2) Remove the V-belts. <Ref. to ME(H4DOTC)-75, REMOVAL, V-belt.>

3) When inspecting #1 and #3 cylinders

(1) Remove the rocker cover RH. <Ref. to ME(H4DOTC)-147, ROCKER COVER RH, REMOVAL, Rocker Cover.>

NOTE:

When working on the vehicle, place a suitable container under the vehicle.

(2) Set #1 cylinder piston to top dead center of compression stroke by rotating the crank pulley clockwise using the socket wrench.

> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> When the timing mark (A) on crank pulley is aligned to the 0° in timing gauge (B) on chain cover as shown in the figure, the #1 cylinder piston is located at TDC of compression stroke if the intake camshaft and exhaust camshaft does not depress the #1 cylinder intake side roller rocker arm (intake valve) and exhaust side roller rocker arm (exhaust valve). If roller rocker arm (valve) is depressed, turn the crank pulley by 360° in order to make #1 cylinder piston at TDC of compression stroke.
>
> ![](images/0a7a1262b1ebe19eccc338e281e4bdd3bab30f8b4c22ed3549c41f9539cbaa0c.jpg)
>
> ME(H4DOTC)-34
>
> (3) Check the cam clearance for #1 cylinder intake, #1 cylinder exhaust and #3 cylinder exhaust. NOTE: • Measure the roller surface of cam base circle and roller rocker arm using thickness gauge (A). • If the measured value is out of standard, take notes of the value in order to adjust the cam clearance later on.
>
> Cam clearance: Intake Standard 0.13+0.02 –0.03 mm (0.0051+0.0008 –0.0012 in) Exhaust Standard 0.220.02 mm (0.00870.0008 in)
>
> ![](images/4c553f4cbe90fabdb1d674c4c572ae08cda98730682140149155a39987fe0ee2.jpg)
>
> (4) Turn the crank pulley by 360°.
>
> ![](images/c0030984371abd74a8ee23d1af76a1181568a95e4e3c119894659e600e0a5c45.jpg)
>
> (5) Check the clearance of #3 cylinder intake.
>
> NOTE:
>
> Measure the roller surface of cam base circle and roller rocker arm using thickness gauge (A).
>
> If the measured value is out of standard, take notes of the value in order to adjust the cam clearance later on.
>
> Cam clearance: Standard 0.13+0.02 –0.03 mm (0.0051+0.0008 –0.0012 in)
>
> ![](images/333d10e23cb52cdfc82f6cbd9f6fb4a609cd727a9804cc3b81d0e9b32b7496e3.jpg)
>
> 4) When inspecting #2 and #4 cylinders (1) Remove the rocker cover LH. <Ref. to ME(H4DOTC)-149, ROCKER COVER LH, REMOVAL, Rocker Cover.>

> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> hen working on the vehicle, place a suitable container under the vehicle.
>
> (2) Set #2 cylinder piston to top dead center of compression stroke by rotating the crank pulley clockwise using the socket wrench.

> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> When the timing mark (A) on crank pulley is aligned to the 0° in timing gauge (B) on chain cover as shown in the figure, the #2 cylinder piston is located at TDC of compression stroke if the intake camshaft and exhaust camshaft does not depress the #2 cylinder intake side roller rocker arm (intake valve) and exhaust side roller rocker arm (exhaust valve). If roller rocker arm (valve) is depressed, turn the crank pulley by 360° in order to make #2 cylinder piston at TDC of compression stroke.
>
> ![](images/48af48153ecae41ca2477b5355d4ac5bc362eb3f338dd9a9877e549c58f94ee6.jpg)

>
> NOTE:
>
> Measure the roller surface of cam base circle and roller rocker arm using thickness gauge (A).
>
> If the measured value is out of standard, take notes of the value in order to adjust the cam clearance later
>

> Cam clearance: Intake Standard 0.13+0.02 –0.03 mm (0.0051+0.0008 –0.0012 in) Exhaust Standard 0.220.02 mm (0.00870.0008 in)

> ![](images/cf853fd929874f10c9c87ca8bdb9fe1005ed0fbe82a31c03266857de3d903b08.jpg)

(4) Turn the crank pulley by 360°.

![](images/90e535bfd93e39da8d3035fd8b9ddf7d9eaa60f73055446dfc3d403d0b7c869c.jpg)

(5) Check the clearance of #4 cylinder intake.

NOTE:
