### A: REMOVAL

1) Shift the select lever to “N” range.
2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Lift up the vehicle.
4) Remove the center exhaust pipe. (Non-turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-14, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
5) Remove the center exhaust pipe (rear). (Turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-30, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
6) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/9355f5c405469ee5c6703a5dd7b2aaa2af3e5f17ab8a3cf08e78d49de31af0dd.jpg)

7) Disconnect the cable from the arm COMPL.

![](images/845c8af4c951ccaacdfb4749510e978a0e9b06924d6fd7086135bab2c03d53b1.jpg)

(A) Adjusting nut (B) Arm COMPL

### Select Lever

8) Raise the claw of clamp and remove the cable.

![](images/26124407a8ba9a6ad35bbbe9883c1489234efdb53cf76dfc8c66410a87543693.jpg)

(A) Claw

9) Lower the vehicle.
10) Shift the select lever to “N” range.
11) Lower the cover grip AT vertically toward the lever.

![](images/bc65d707a4608339202ad6466e8cc495e78919a60e63f6bd2a86fc1490d28615.jpg)

12) Remove the clamp grip pin.

![](images/876a97164a9925f09725463eb3b44ac84dae01ad7cf84e2d5d064b90860f256c.jpg)

13) Remove the grip assembly.

![](images/25f18b0dedee737302258533db0799f18d0b6bd5fc4c3db84b76cc3930582485.jpg)

14) Remove the ornament panel - consoles LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>
15) Remove the cover shift lever. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>
16) Remove the console box assembly. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>

17) Disconnect the connector, and remove the indicator cover from the housing.

![](images/f7a4cc6722573a99d4be98e67b1067b607c1479ed36dff4a58a405b6243bcd70.jpg)

18) Remove the panel center LWR LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>
19) Remove the housing with the blind A and blind B.

![](images/66073a6d951a8d62f3675d1a72cf5274d70ad0371b42ad2944535c06e3d9ea83.jpg)

20) Remove the blind B.

![](images/e1607f5b0fdd454dbfc89c79bb9020b8d9fb511f56aac2bf51d2ebecc2542b10.jpg)

(A) Blind B (B) Blind A

21) Remove the blind A from the housing.

![](images/320a208c1ee86690a5a4b1bf5c73832742d1aeb994cb3182684545e93d50f7b9.jpg)

22) Remove the harness clip from the select lever assembly.

![](images/42e3a56e14d5ebf30e3bd9f3eed675d364c64907ed3ecd9d7c89f3c550af0f37.jpg)

CS-01668

23) Disconnect the harness connector.

![](images/ac949f9b6ccc8060763172187a3c9137a20b079caed9fef4a2d3a6bbcb0ee9e8.jpg)

24) Remove the four bolts to remove the select lever assembly.

![](images/bac0353e283d5d1257ebc3fb1537277ba5c04abe4f2d752a06ba4663d48ce2c3.jpg)

CS-01669

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Set the select lever assembly to the vehicle body.
2) Tighten the four mounting bolts to attach the select lever assembly to the vehicle body.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/290bd59e5289525d3940f371a4163308709f1796e1794483a61e0593969e2808.jpg)

CS-01669

3) Connect the harness connector.

![](images/e0a002e2894205ac410ead8da324baa74db5185b2cfefc1fe7026ebd6306384e.jpg)

4) Install the harness clip to the select lever assembly.
5) Shift the select lever to “N” range.
6) Install the blind A to the housing.

NOTE:

The blind A should be installed so that it is securely caught inside the tab of the housing.

![](images/5ab58670d8648419a61733c1e0a515e558aec868d44d3770f70cf13370247d81.jpg)

7) Install the blind B behind the blind A.

![](images/3c051d64b496b123cc95996f1788a6cb424e725746d699270a1668d3c443e320.jpg)

(A) Blind B (B) Blind A

8) Install the housing.

![](images/1164393596218139c7b6aa80d0a3c9cd649cbb887fee71c0db74cf5f7d8d11aa.jpg)

9) Install the panel center LWR LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console Box.>

10) Install the indicator cover, then connect the connector.

![](images/448d8d72d190a7c00f7ebb2b86301a535a50823b5aea2d9ecbb885244324500f.jpg)

11) Install the console box assembly. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console Box.>
12) Install the cover - shift lever. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console Box.>
13) Install the ornament panel consoles LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console Box.>
14) Accessing from the button side of the grip, attach the clamp grip pin.

![](images/add2a0572032f9f5eeee19a02477fcc4c607d72350da47cf94573a534901bb50.jpg)

15) Install the cover grip AT securely.

NOTE: After installation, check that the cover grip AT cannot be detached.

![](images/68b481f8407d21dcaf2c15f909344d5433a8f54c3dfa14f4dcd63cca6851daed.jpg)

CS-01435

16) Insert the grip assembly to the select lever and press it down until a click is heard.

![](images/7eb8769e29dde579950ebb063bb2ca3b93d68ef052d6516a96f355cf47c4b4ed.jpg)

17) After installation of grip, check the following points.
• The grip will not come off.
The button on the grip operates normally.
18) Shift the select lever to “N” range.
19) Lift up the vehicle.
20) Secure the cable to the bracket. <Ref. to CS-48, INSTALLATION, Select Cable.>
21) Adjust the select cable position. <Ref. to CS-52, ADJUSTMENT, Select Cable.>
22) After adjustment, confirm that the select lever operates properly at all range positions using the shift lock release button.

23) Install the center exhaust cover.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/6db04d4f8baa33c3d1299eec910a4fb432baebad7e0bad72079b95dded31bad6.jpg)

24) Install the center exhaust pipe. (Non-turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-15, INSTALLATION, Center Ex
haust Pipe.>
25) Install the center exhaust pipe (rear). (Turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-35, INSTALLATION, Center
Exhaust Pipe.>
26) Lower the vehicle.
27) Connect the battery ground terminal.

### B: INSTALLATION

28) Inspect the following items. If a malfunction is found in the inspection, adjust the select cable or inhibitor
switch. (1) The shift lock operates normally. <Ref. to CS-13, SHIFT LOCK OPERATION, INSPECTION, AT Shift Lock Control System.> (2) Engine starts when the select lever is in “P” or “N” range, but not in other ranges. (3) Back-up light illuminates when the select lever is in the “R” range, but not in other ranges. (4) Select lever and indicator positions are matched.

### 1. GRIP ASSY

1) Remove the button assembly_AT.

![](images/9aa5b1007dd55e1e7d9a3b00f0d6f100dc25de90b1dca104de2912bff4b39dfb.jpg)

(A) Claw

2) Remove the rod COMPL.

### 2. AT SELECT LEVER ASSEMBLY

1) Remove the spacer plate.

![](images/daa0ad4b5ebb458973252bed4308469de26cf6427dead7996af4b940dbf2bdc0.jpg)

2) Remove the gasket.

![](images/b397ecccc16fd98419fac988591d20f98a2f0fcce77a5a4bbbae40d1aed87dad.jpg)

3) Insert a flat tip screwdriver with a thin tip under the connector and disconnect the harness connector from the plate COMPL.

![](images/f1f997c1b2b0674e7a50fc86ac6d4332c094d12300cce88be25ddaa2e07c8dfe.jpg)

4) Remove the harness from the plate COMPL.

![](images/52b8ed50925eb76482c5b0953b7f2c07bcaaa1a0385a1470064dbcb8dc4b3d0f.jpg)

5) Raise the claw with a flat tip screwdriver with a thin tip and remove the solenoid unit.

![](images/1344cb7bca44d284d9d6756a29538d62dc0117056d634cea163bbeaa2df0d41d.jpg)

6) Using a flat tip screwdriver with a thin tip, remove the solenoid unit terminals from the connector.

![](images/a2a2ce09daf2017a023809e2fc3ad6ba0356d73e37fe3f7fd0844c31dcb2d167.jpg)

(A) Solenoid unit terminals

7) Remove the clamp push nut. NOTE: Replace the clamp push nut with a new part.

![](images/69dbed650033f1ac8e39834850c8f133d1a990700c4c65df9503a7dd7530de6c.jpg)

8) Pull out shaft control.

![](images/5ada420919fee5679806a25dfa1e059e597de1d434071bf6181ac768bbafff70.jpg)

9) Remove the clamp push nut.

NOTE: Replace the clamp push nut with a new part.

![](images/5025dfef92421d3949aecd8f797068131e153e6389dcb2ebf3a672ef1cff71e4.jpg)

10) Pull out spacer pin guide.

![](images/1fce896602bd0943725d58d1b63ebb844cd8fce2a6926a98276dd8092a82ffa9.jpg)

CS-01114

11) Remove the clamp pin.

![](images/b313ad3341c25e9145020e35783186ada3237ec977f96a8b654774aee1f18cf4.jpg)

CS-01628

12) Remove the spacer pin guide.

![](images/2540db5d9346a394f69d25c1622003dc4f5fc9225279253c99cd467240e379b0.jpg)

13) Remove the select lever COMPL from the plate COMPL.

![](images/4912013ef25d504fdd14c005c6234651c55cf6d3fb92c6d52b58e998d324ce44.jpg)

14) Remove the arm COMPL.

![](images/f521d6184de17e0328dc2d45246f808ae095511e144df47461c8ef57d707018c.jpg)

(A) Arm COMPL (B) Selector lever COMPL

15) Remove the plate guide from the select lever COMPL.

![](images/d664d6085d4653cf9e7300b945906dffa2653d0b1ec8f1c31d8847dfd14da1db.jpg)

16) Remove the rod detent and detent spring from the select lever COMPL.

![](images/9d12c0ed5214e680d0832479432ae3185bf69190ffed61c045894f7602dce500.jpg)

### D: ASSEMBLY

1) Clean all the parts before assembly.
2) Apply Multemp D or equivalent to the sliding portion of each part.
3) Assemble in the reverse order of disassembly.

NOTE: Insert the solenoid unit terminals to the harness connector.

![](images/5d83305e90c353c83050eba90d4eeef147af2bbd15b14c091aec35abd59dccb5.jpg)

CS-01551

(A) Solenoid unit (color code: blue) (B) Solenoid unit (color code: black)

4) After installation, check the following points.

• The select indicator matches the select lever position when the select lever is changed from “P” range to
“D” range.
• The select lever position and the position mark match each other. Operating force to move the select lever from “P” to “D” range.

### E: INSPECTION

1) Inspect the removed parts by comparing with new parts for deformation, damage and wear. Repair or replace if defective. 2) Inspect the select lever assembly operating condition before assembly. Normal if it operates smoothly.

### A: REMOVAL

1) Shift the select lever to “N” range.
2) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
3) Lift up the vehicle.
4) Remove the center exhaust pipe. (Non-turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-14, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
5) Remove the center exhaust pipe (rear). (Turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-30, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
6) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/216c735f998f4f2eca7b7367441806a3f4cd20fe14c7ca0877a9c0261732f4cc.jpg)

7) Remove the snap pin and washer from the shifter arm.

![](images/6506dae6ffde48f60f2d3f228b39446986678eb926143da7a83b12a0796685c4.jpg)

(A) Shifter arm (C) Select cable (D) Washer (B) Snap pin

8) Remove the plate assembly from the transmission case.

![](images/9a63a5e4575fb5707230a5777fe10877705e12a7ecc8f3b16c4a778698087261.jpg)

(A) Select cable (B) Plate ASSY

9) Disconnect the cable from arm COMPL.

![](images/e3de4022f3a051ad1d39c236af32e5940d57b1c97fbc97cb8713916b4f491d07.jpg)

(A) Adjusting nut (B) Arm COMPL

10) Raise the claw of clamp to remove the cable from bracket.

![](images/4a6b1639b282e7852a6891a083e883bb591847a85dbb1606027a9157f7d8935f.jpg)

(A) Claw

11) Remove the select cable from plate assembly.

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Position the select cable as shown in the figure, and install it to the plate assembly.

CAUTION:

• If the cable is installed in the wrong direction, loosen the bracket bolts, and then reinstall the cable in the correct direction. • Do not forcibly turn the cable (wire side) to align the direction correctly.

Tightening torque: T: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/a5b41251501cfe1b24c8e36b98fb9628b95ae33996d6d4f109c29556548c21bd.jpg)

(A) Select cable

2) Install the select cable to the shifter arm.

3) Install the plate assembly to transmission.

Tightening torque: T: 25 N·m (2.5 kgf-m, 18.4 ft-lb)

![](images/ef49c9c180bf113c44d3e2fde888e81f85c44b06d8b002fb330c010d1910a6b0.jpg)

CS-01540

(A) Select cable (B) Plate ASSY

4) Install the washer and snap pin to the shifter arm.

![](images/9fe34cd422d70fd1c43f474e1a6b639532e8f635753d7f0a3f95dd11cdf7ab92.jpg)

(A) Shifter arm (C) Select cable (D) Washer (B) Snap pin

5) Install new clamp paying attention to the installing direction.

![](images/6da985ff279f672a3d8a5e784849b1d90d3abd8b096f6b5a8d0950fc29bea66c.jpg)

(A) Clamp (B) Forward

6) Insert the tip of inner cable into connector hole of select lever, and fix the cable to bracket.

![](images/04076a3ab2bc7077e9a441ab008c0ccde25c28f5b8d0c9349310df34fe81961b.jpg)

7) Shift the select lever to the “N” range, and then adjust the select cable position. <Ref. to CS-52, ADJUSTMENT, Select Cable.>

8) Install the center exhaust cover.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/fc81d6d5525ede9aef4c15ed5ae6a1f4b49b8446b8d08a3d2c1e03b44a344177.jpg)

9) Install the center exhaust pipe. (Non-turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-15, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
10) Install the center exhaust pipe (rear). (Turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-35, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
11) Lower the vehicle.
12) Connect the battery ground terminal.

### C: INSPECTION

Check the removed cable and replace or adjust if damaged, rusty or malfunctioning.

1) Check the cable for smooth operation.
2) Check the inner cable for damage and rust.
3) Check the outer cable for damage, bends and cracks.
4) Check the boot for damage, cracks and deterioration.
5) Move the select lever from “P” to “D” range. Check the existence of feel to contact the detents in each
range. If the detents cannot be felt or the position pointer is improperly aligned, adjust the cable.
6) Check if the starter motor rotates when the select lever is set to “P” range.
7) Check the back-up light illumination when the select lever is in “R” range.
8) Check the parking lock operation when the select lever is in “P” range.

### D: ADJUSTMENT

1) Shift the select lever to “N” range.
2) Lift up the vehicle.
3) Remove the center exhaust pipe. (Non-turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-14, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
4) Remove the center exhaust pipe (rear). (Turbo model) <Ref. to EX(H4DOTC)-30, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
5) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/3af8ad0f8b11bc3eaeb514e8ce9436663d2944e13a92a65f2c867ef381782b3c.jpg)

6) Loosen the adjusting nuts on both sides.

![](images/c7f7f3b71a1609cbea5645c2c17c82e20f597a10e10d3aed15dfbe4b114e47ec.jpg)

(A) Adjusting nut A (B) Adjusting nut B

7) Turn adjusting nut B until it lightly touches the connector.

![](images/0ca80a8dd57c3258bd87e9c8f08d303f481afcf6c3256c6657c4eb01773753f2.jpg)

(A) Forward side (C) Connector (E) Contact point (B) Select lever (D) Adjusting nut B (F) Adjusting nut A

8) Set a spanner wrench to adjusting nut B so that i t does not rotate, and then tighten the adjusting nut A.

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/a327c697be1175f5284137b444896603ff52674ec2158ff9d1c86d31cf8176fd.jpg)

(A) Adjusting nut A (B) Adjusting nut B

9) After the completion of adjustment, confirm that the select lever operates normally at all ranges.
10) Installing procedure hereafter is in the reverse order of removal.

### 1. SOLENOID UNIT

1) Remove the AT select lever. <Ref. to CS-24, REMOVAL, Select Lever.>
2) Remove the spacer and gasket. <Ref. to CS-36, DISASSEMBLY, Select Lever.>
3) Using a flat tip screwdriver with a thin tip, remove the harness connector from the plate COMPL.

![](images/199500e1730627317dd789cd743c525d9c66b6ca9b37e45c847566d72d3e2c24.jpg)
4) Raise the claw using a flat tip screwdriver with a thin tip, and remove the solenoid unit from the plate COMPL.

![](images/75af9b874ebbc0ecd081ab0a1ec37a9a51269d2300da591eca8194c1e7cc63b0.jpg)

5) Using a flat tip screwdriver with a thin tip, remove the solenoid unit terminals from the harness connector.

![](images/109414b0ba4603691828c64696bfa47dda568082d5fd6840e6f5802fa0969708.jpg)

(A) Solenoid unit terminals

### 2. “P” RANGE SWITCH

For the removal of “P” range switch, refer to the procedure for AT select lever. <Ref. to CS-36, DISASSEMBLY, Select Lever.>

### B: INSTALLATION

Install in the reverse order of removal.

NOTE: Insert the solenoid unit terminals to the harness connector.

![](images/ec035cdcd6d6b005089a8eca13c36a32b46018d3fb8303fdd67fe1e973ac0f5e.jpg)

(A) Solenoid unit (color code: blue) (B) Solenoid unit (color code: black)

### 6. Body Integrated Unit

A: NOTE Refer to “Body Integrated Unit” for removal and installation procedure. <Ref. to SL-74, Body Integrated Unit.>

### A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
2) Lift up the vehicle.
3) Remove the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-14, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
4) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/e6bf0f20cb3b9f3bb314bcb88934c8e01aa14b4bf67b749b5135834fcbc7b1ea.jpg)

5) Remove the cable cover plate.

![](images/1da246a1bb26d2e43cf8868888ef0f8df524957b1fdefa1ceb1f5d4094b55a38.jpg)

6) Disconnect the MT gear shift cable and MT gear select cable from the gear shift lever assembly.

### Be careful not to deform the cable inner.

(1) Pull out down the MT gear shift cable to spread the spring.
(2) Push the MT gear select cable in the direction of arrow, and remove it.

![](images/a335addb14b1d489481b0ae61f1a6583dbc1d9cb92758b85c610f68457615e1e.jpg)

(A) MT gear shift cable (B) MT gear select cable

7) Remove the cable cover assembly.

![](images/8d44276d94d4a2d673cea357765043d5be341bf843e47dda1f7e461e81564edc.jpg)

8) Lower the vehicle.
9) Remove the ornament panel consoles LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>
10) Remove the gear shift knob and remove the cover shift lever. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>
11) Remove the console box assembly. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>
12) Remove the panel center LWR LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-65, REMOVAL, Console Box.>
13) Remove the harness clamp.

14) Remove the gear shift lever assembly mounting bolt and remove the gear shift lever assembly from the vehicle.

![](images/995d091f88c3b28de10fdb46949eaeaaa2dd81ec56e9c64494036080abec0d77.jpg)

CS-01672

### B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the gear shift lever assembly.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/690ccf5411580b7d457d88ab1ea705622f4263694b1b14c4b1d93da32de27152.jpg)

2) Install the harness clamp.
3) Lift up the vehicle.

4) Install the cable cover assembly.

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/dfc89cf8c81a1fc6e27f27b4c5237ed502a156546c72b59f35c64a73cc7c32e2.jpg)

5) Connect the MT gear shift cable and MT gear select cable.

CAUTION: Be careful not to deform the cable inner.

![](images/61019ea0c2932783b76fded2af0f36a361ce2c5ed0139c77749fcee7b8e3e8c2.jpg)

(A) MT gear shift cable (B) MT gear select cable

6) Attach the cable cover plate.

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/3152fe5a8c7cfed1434d753aac01bd5a82e9dc29f407451eff92c1cbad7ce802.jpg)

7) Install the center exhaust cover.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/bdaffa6951a456d836b68aabf599f17a8ff868e48414fa4dd19f629f248cdba1.jpg)

8) Install the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-15, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
9) Lower the vehicle.
10) Install the panel center LWR LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console Box.>
11) Install the console box assembly. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console Box.>
12) Install the cover shift lever, and install the gear shift knob. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console
Box.>
13) Install the ornament panel consoles LH and RH. <Ref. to EI-68, INSTALLATION, Console Box.>
14) Make sure the gears can be shifted accurately into each gear. Adjust the MT gear select lever, if the
gears cannot be shifted correctly. <Ref. to CS-89, ADJUSTMENT, MT Gear Select Cable.>
15) Connect the battery ground terminal.

### C: INSPECTION

1) Check the parts for deformation, damage and wear. Repair or replace if necessary. Compare the removed
parts with new parts to confirm if there are damages or not.
2) Check that selecting to the reverse direction is disable unless the slider is pulled up.
3) Check that selecting to the reverse direction is possible when the slider is pulled up to the full.
4) Check that the shift lever moves to initial position, when the slider backs to “N” position from step 3).

![](images/a166dc01dba254829534df292b3add3b426f76157c269fa94a03247af04004f7.jpg)

### 8. MT Gear Shift Cable

A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
2) Lift up the vehicle.
3) Remove the transmission under cover.
4) Remove the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-14, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
5) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/c516635979cbf14e155b2494990518375fe95bfaeb6571ae320b2e9263d5fef0.jpg)

![](images/062f60d682d217f7e19a72bc14f1516ea675ea1f3703a34b19f39eea6ee278d4.jpg)

6) Remove the cable clamp and take out the MT gear shift cable from the clamp.

![](images/33645602d7ec4065917702bb8a9a6be02dd3d07512d9991c99934d8a529cd8fc.jpg)

(A) Cable clamp

7) Remove the dust cover from transmission body.

![](images/2af2b1dff1cc40dee764ad31b56d67b3dc571e3808d3585a724fb21e8216c558.jpg)

(A) Dust cover

8) Remove the snap pin from the shift lever COMPL.

![](images/29ab8b8e0d75cec17f81e25f873a3588c4687279dbcc7f807f964443d61d2f20.jpg)

(A) Snap pin

9) Remove the bolts holding the shift bracket.

![](images/2858893a8fb990378b5fd90f233d4ab27c93a4bcbd6cfaf93184a9da7e56ad42.jpg)

(A) Shift bracket

10) Remove the shift bracket and MT gear shift cable as a single unit from the transmission body.

![](images/e6f0c704df6825a62c9b35c37710286b0b578ecb97bedc6d0582d6ceb9a586ea.jpg)

(A) MT gear shift cable (B) Shift bracket

11) Remove the cable cover plate.

![](images/fbff1d3aa24eefc91cdaba85c56648b1764d9a296d3aba923b93a3b5e946d671.jpg)

12) Disconnect the MT gear shift cable.

### CAUTION: Be careful not to deform the cable inner.

NOTE: Pull out down the MT gear shift cable to spread the spring.

![](images/be21698abf79e58ee711b3043cd1e69d530fe79b730bfca77d5395f9b5236b88.jpg)

(A) MT gear shift cable

13) Remove the clamp which holds the MT gear shift cable.

![](images/5f75a569103160e215f0dc6966b5effcaf681f1bb3a722aa87053fa9c5a698a2.jpg)

(A) Clamp (B) MT gear shift cable

14) Pull out the MT gear shift cable from cable cover assembly.

![](images/e3d789e2ef347cfd49d143333ea91c61d28c99591b721a6e160445f1b78368ab.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

CAUTION:

Do not bend MT gear shift cable at a sharp angle. • When replacing the new MT gear shift cable, secure it to shift bracket with the clamps, be careful not to mistake the installing direction.

![](images/9aaee20a37e627d4713e195c41b79ab8d475f7b6b155f912a22ebbc68b05d824.jpg)

(A) Old MT gear shift cable (B) New MT gear shift cable (C) Shift bracket

1) Install the MT gear shift cable and shift bracket as a single unit onto transmission.

![](images/ec05f043119c4ef5674be4ba460ab4925f3991a71573e6b374411708e721923d.jpg)

(A) MT gear shift cable (B) Shift bracket

2) Tighten the shift bracket with specified torque.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/cfdf0d46d90cb0b8afef46cbca4a9f69e918d5047b7b2f687f193904b5c48fb0.jpg)

(A) Shift bracket

3) Install the snap pin to the shift lever COMPL.

![](images/dd6c4fcc294a54e3477fcd0cba1048de2299d3ec74285ad836c9b5ff19ea7dc9.jpg)

(A) Snap pin

4) Install the dust cover to the transmission body.

Tightening torque: 15 N·m (1.5 kgf-m, 11.1 ft-lb)

![](images/9aa4fefdde9c615fda2ee4dc25e008e9008de18f4736e6ac1994ffb9a141b922.jpg)

5) Insert the MT gear shift cable into cable cover assembly, and secure it with the clamp.

![](images/ff2700013b8b747bd507434d7ca19c42083dc97422bdc838dacd1bcdd89a6fed.jpg)

(A) Clamp (B) MT gear shift cable

6) Connect the MT gear shift cable.
7) Attach the cable cover plate.

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/96827283ea4e1528cbf2fd0df4f0f433057b394188f60f14810eb23d8ae01d1d.jpg)

8) Insert the MT gear shift cable into cable clamp, and install to the transmission.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/f0cf5959c7fa14c4f522332a3f53e2956982d7ebabee83e2fd7d3e0d304a5a19.jpg)

(A) Cable clamp

9) Install the center exhaust cover.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/7fa4a203434804f89eb944759cb21c9f4f90753ec39738e8dc5d421af35c490c.jpg)

10) Install the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-15, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.>

11) Install the transmission under cover.

![](images/bea1fcb61418ee10319e9eeae8941748d33744a910fe159607941b49d129cf89.jpg)

12) Lower the vehicle.
13) Connect the battery ground terminal.
14) Make sure the gears can be shifted accurately into each gear.

### 9. MT Gear Select Cable

A: REMOVAL

CAUTION:

Always use new MT gear select cable if the cable is removed from selector lever COMPL of transmission side.

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery.
2) Remove the clip (A) from the air intake boot.
3) Loosen the clamp (B) connecting the air intake boot and air cleaner case (rear).
4) Loosen the clamp (C) which connects the air intake boot and throttle body.

![](images/7100277690adb05e507ac3a2064db934d5f9c9c2adb0a4de47ab5fdf69f90ad1.jpg)

5) Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body, and move it to the left side wheel apron.

![](images/19e0db55d0bd182306a309714a418a5ff1e83a8e04025a99a5b979c2791a4e23.jpg)

6) Disconnect the engine harness connectors, then remove the harness bracket.

![](images/6921e50a02ff88a82395add693f883be72eb8524fff2c6d313d479d28a596b0d.jpg)

(A) Engine harness connectors (B) Harness bracket

7) Disconnect the transmission radio ground cord terminal.

![](images/d6ac9172236e641978ada7428e91d90db35807a463320b03667c238e35e022c6.jpg)

8) Remove the pitching stopper.

![](images/3f8fe03a4d1b0b024367d0f9184a3380a3c415804fd21f8666384864792a5ba2.jpg)

9) Lift up the vehicle.
10) Remove the transmission under cover.

![](images/47dc95d1ce2ca028172fb06fece1317a03f1e319250acdd425557003ae1b2432.jpg)

11) Remove the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-14, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>

12) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/e7e45fddee31f6b5807ed233d9163f1b66667b421363ebb7ad204685a600e5de.jpg)

13) Remove the propeller shaft. <Ref. to DS-11, REMOVAL, Propeller Shaft.>
14) Remove the cable clamp and take out the MT gear select cable from the cla

![](images/c531f2c822d99b536e8e904aeffddb056ce02ba6118e3c71949b94dee6f9871a.jpg)

(A) Cable clamp

15) Place the transmission jack under the transmission.

16) Remove the mounting bolt of front crossmember and rear crossmember, and lower the transmission approx. 100 mm (4 in).

![](images/e91e13d0db24e1a576dae60db1790b8cbf9f8ff42b251ad66c8b6c473446cde1.jpg)

17) Insert a spanner between the selector lever COMPL and the MT gear select cable, and remove the MT gear select cable by raising the handle.

NOTE:

Use a spanner with 11 to 13 in size.
The thickness of the spanner must not exceed 6 mm (0.2 in).

![](images/a919c1b5d91302ee81d1349a8b8c1ce4aa82f2402991c759f1664455ebb363a7.jpg)

(A) MT gear select cable (B) Spanner (C) Forward

18) Remove the MT gear select cable and select bracket as a single unit from the transmission body.

![](images/80dab052e77164befbd8605ec746c74194213b33608c28f6c192d0ddf166b28a.jpg)

(A) MT gear select cable (B) Select bracket

19) Remove the cable cover plate.

![](images/7d81cefb058fe3262743d1f2c9709d5b2fc045d332c143c05b6f7e6fec4698c3.jpg)

20) Disconnect the MT gear select cable.

### CAUTION: Be careful not to deform the cable inner.

NOTE: Push the MT gear select cable in the direction of arrow, and remove it.

![](images/8df1da2733322699f93b3fb0df8f1d74c874a789c3a8c0b2b1c5574928877fd6.jpg)

(A) MT gear select cable

21) Remove the clamp which holds the MT gear select cable.

![](images/c00d04e34610d826461d0b2b50258f1ddb7a19977bd61a83cd02df4a2603fb2d.jpg)

(A) Clamp (B) MT gear select cable

22) Pull out the MT gear select cable from cable cover assembly.

CAUTION: Do not bend the MT gear select cable sharply.

![](images/f118f83b10480b2a2a298a894d43c366edb0327219441c659383eb3adaedce8f.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

CAUTION:

• Always use new MT gear select cable if the cable is removed from selector lever COMPL of transmission side.
• Do not bend the MT gear select cable sharply.
• Do not twist the inner cable excessively.
1) Remove the MT gear select cable from the select bracket.

CAUTION: Check for assembling position before removing the MT gear select cable from the select bracket.

![](images/2e7e5d345236614e33c097c2d4fdbcf405346095c249e1ca6d0df4bf43d4ad92.jpg)

(A) MT gear select cable (B) Select bracket

2) Set to the new MT gear select cable to the select bracket and secure it with the clamp. CAUTION: Be careful not to mistake the MT gear select cable installing direction.

![](images/df66333025e43c730ab81955b1f8bae02040ecdd7b81fbe7845df71a3a8659c0.jpg)

(A) MT gear select cable (B) Select bracket (C) Clamp

3) Install the MT gear select cable and select bracket as a single unit to the transmission body.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/78df1239cf81f2668e1b6eb1679e90f26a530ee26692c027951f6b927d38026f.jpg)

(A) Select bracket (B) MT gear select cable

4) Install the MT gear select cable to the select lever COMPL.

![](images/89e7c1382a97996a5e684655bae346be30bd32531ca3059d22645000b9a3169d.jpg)

(A) MT gear select cable (B) Select bracket

5) Insert the MT gear select cable into cable cover assembly, and secure it with the clamp.

![](images/8ec22f617b974502dd1fb0da1229e8011696f8e340ac879a14b19b44795b08ec.jpg)

(A) Clamp (B) MT gear select cable

6) Measure the exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable. If out of specification, adjust the MT gear select cable. <Ref. to CS-89, ADJUSTMENT, MT Gear Select Cable.>

Exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable: Specification: 11 mm (0.4 in)

![](images/438efa8e4936e42e53e0216dadeff9d83b95e8628f9dbfed6e2fd5ba019ade86.jpg)

7) Connect the MT gear select cable.
8) Attach the cable cover plate.

Tightening torque: 7.5 N·m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

![](images/f925df3bcb31a9ec7b1070d19a9a2d50b954118688eb4898d9f38653abdb1638.jpg)

9) Insert the MT gear select cable into cable clamp, and install to the transmission.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/4069441860cdbfec5c40406787fceb373819bfcc7ccbb939a29244b48684c621.jpg)

(A) Cable clamp

10) Raise the transmission jack, install the front crossmember and rear crossmember.

Tightening torque: T1: 70 N·m (7.1 kgf-m, 51.6 ft-lb) T2: 140 N·m (14.3 kgf-m, 103.3 ft-lb)

![](images/74153edf3a25dbd4cbe8a70f01183b8d47bcc796173a7fac7d1d68a0d46b9b89.jpg)

11) Take out the transmission jack.
12) Install the propeller shaft. <Ref. to DS-13, INSTALLATION, Propeller Shaft.>

13) Install the center exhaust cover.

Tightening torque: 18 N·m (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/38bfb636e08c57a1d98434545ac79e78a1b46b3b74b1abcd582adeede0f84d40.jpg)

14) Install the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-15, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.>
15) Install the transmission under cover.

![](images/5881e7269a76bbb3103c719744626d62c85241a3ac8fef2e6f411e20f74c0106.jpg)

### B: INSTALLATION

16) Lower the vehicle.
17) Install the pitching stopper. <Ref. to 6MT-34, PITCHING STOPPER, INSTALLATION, Transmission Mounting System.>

18) Install the transmission radio ground cord terminal.

Tightening torque: 13 N·m (1.3 kgf-m, 9.6 ft-lb)

![](images/44bb5dfc0e8e635b6b05d269f2224de25e725012feb34839cf68da1daaab6f4d.jpg)

19) Connect the engine harness connector, then attach the harness bracket.

![](images/ebc7085e31f966ddef25a467a402f194b2bd39a5568c4ed8d7d8630bc87404fc.jpg)

(A) Engine harness connectors (B) Harness bracket

20) Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H4DO)-11, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.>
21) Connect the battery ground terminal.
22) Make sure the gears can be shifted accurately into each gear.

### Exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable: Specification: 11 mm (0.4 in)

![](images/1b4881ebc13216b58d732f26509dd9e0cd91963767aaba4d5ad26a6cc8e12916.jpg)

2) If it is not within the specification, perform the adjustment. <Ref. to CS-89, ADJUSTMENT, MT Gear Select Cable.>

### D: ADJUSTMENT

NOTE:

Two person are required to perform the MT gear select cable adjustment. (Only the step 7) requires two workers.)
1) Shift the select lever to the 6th.
2) Remove the cable cover plate.

![](images/8c6e35889464419b9b70c92aee2eb1d1ae5f5ff7527b6cc6c271798b5ddedfae.jpg)

3) Disconnect the MT gear select cable.

NOTE: Push the MT gear select cable in the direction of arrow, and remove it.

![](images/e72830bc0425c10c1b17541048752878e62d05625dd3990ae0578e99bc9dc0c5.jpg)

(A) MT gear select cable

4) Measure the exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable.

![](images/15d666b6010c4943b503ff7e8143aff73ced1eadca74e828de10ab564e50bb4d.jpg)

(a) Measurement value

5) Slide the slider (green) in the direction of the arrow and release the lock piece (pink) by using flat tip screwdriver etc.

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> Lock piece is easily damaged for the resin. When the lock piece is broken, replace the new MT gear select cable.
>
> NOTE:
>
> Rotate the MT gear select cable to 180 degrees, slide the slider in the direction of the arrow and push the claw of lock piece.
>
> ![](images/7a80283fc5a52c692e5607d25ef5f5f5b9a6a9b32e39dada0869578c13045bb1.jpg)
>
> (A) Slider (C) Claw (D) Flat tip screwdriver (B) Lock piece
>
> 6) Connect the MT gear select cable to the select lever, with the lock piece released.
>
> ![](images/c8dbeade1dcd889fdbbb91c9b300e776e1f0681d37e8e5c4a29d30ed34b58567.jpg)
>
> (A) Lock piece (B) Select lever (C) MT gear select cable
>
> 7) Move the select lever to the Rev side, keep the exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable to 11 mm (0.4 in), and push the lock piece.
>
> NOTE: Pull up the slider of the gear shift lever assembly, move to the Rev side.
>
> ![](images/5c87a97c5128457c7796e5094e23aba13f3d826716be971c6338cacf4ca1d8a2.jpg)
>
> (a) Exposed length 11 mm (0.4 in)
>
> (A) Lock piece (B) Select lever (C) MT gear select cable
>
> 8) Shift to 5th  6th and Rev, and check for stuck.
> 9) If no fault is found in the shift and select operation, restore the vehicle.
> 10) If the shifting operation is not smooth, readjust the exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable by referring to the following figure.
>
> ![](images/d79ddc39c1ab0720eb7338dae8bbceb407ef9580ea1bebcdc7b081a4c3f2b354.jpg)
>
> (a) Exposed length of MT gear select cable
> (A) Extend direction of exposed (B) Shorten direction of exposed (C) Specification of exposed length length of MT gear select cable length of MT gear select cable (a)

### MT Gear Select Cable

• If the shift cannot be inserted to push the reverse lock bracket 5th and 6th.
→ Extend the exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable. When operate the select lever to 4th  5th, it cannot be operated at select lever crank line.
→ Shorten the exposed length (a) of MT gear select cable.

NOTE: If it cannot adjust, replace the MT gear select cable.

### C: CAUTION

• Wear appropriate work clothing, including a cap, protective goggles and protective shoes when performing any work.

Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation or disassembly.

Keep the disassembled parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.

• Do not place the valve cover with its inner side facing up until it is installed, to prevent intrusion of foreign matter into the control valve body.

• Before removal, installation or disassembly, be sure to clarify the failure. Avoid unnecessary removal, installation, disassembly and replacement.

• When disassembling the case and other light alloy parts, use a plastic hammer to force it apart. Do not pry apart with screwdrivers or other tools.

Vehicle components are extremely hot after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts.

Use SUBARU genuine CVTF and recommended grease. Do not mix CVTF, grease etc. of different grades or manufacturers.

Be sure to tighten bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

Place lifts, shop jacks or rigid racks at specified locations.

Apply CVTF onto sliding or revolving surfaces before installation

Replace deformed or damaged snap rings with new parts.

Before installing O-rings or oil seals, apply sufficient amount of CVTF or gear oil to appropriate locations n order to avoid damage and deformation.

Be careful not to incorrectly install or fail to install O-rings, snap rings and other such parts.

• Before securing a part on a vise, place cushioning material such as wood blocks, aluminum plate, or cloth between the part and the vise.

Avoid damaging the mating surface of the case.

Before applying liquid gasket, completely remove the old liquid gasket.

• After removing the sensors, breather hose and plugs, plug the holes to avoid foreign materials intruding as necessary.

• During disassembly or assembly, be sure to use nylon gloves or paper towels. Do not use cloth gloves or waste cloth.

### A: INSPECTION

Check for leakage of CVTF from transmission.

B: ADJUSTMENT

CAUTION:

• CVTF level changes along with CVTF temperature. When inspecting CVTF level, observe the specified CVTF temperature.

Always use specified CVTF. Using other fluid will cause malfunction.

1) Lift up the vehicle.
2) Remove the under cover front transmission.
3) Idle the engine to raise CVTF temperature to 35 — 45°C (95 — 113°F) on Subaru Select Monitor.
4) Operate the select lever in P  R  N  D and D  N  R  P to circulate CVTF with the engine idling.
5) With the engine running, lift up the vehicle and remove the filler plug.

### Pay special attention to the following operations as the engine is at idle.

NOTE: CVTF is at the specified level when it is up to the filler plug hole lower section.

### Specified fluid:

<Ref. to CVT(TR580)-4, HYDRAULIC CONTROL AND LUBRICATION, SPECIFICATION, General Description.>

CAUTION:

Note that when CVTF is added up to the lower section of filler plug while the transmission is in cold condition, overfilling of CVTF occurs, causing the oil to spill out.

### 4. AWD ON/OFF Switching Mode A: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

Follow the messages displayed on the Subaru Select Monitor when working.
Perform as necessary in FWD mode.
When switched to FWD, AWD light illuminates.

### B: PROCEDURE

CAUTION:

• Do not turn the power of the Subaru Select Monitor OFF during work, and do not disconnect the data link connector.

On completing the work in FWD, switch back in AWD.

1) Shift the select lever to “P” range.
2) Connect the Subaru Select Monitor to data link connector.
3) Turn the ignition switch to ON. (For model with push button start, press the push button ignition switch twice without depressing brake pedal.)
4) Turn off all switches causing an electrical load, such as headlights, A/C, seat heater and rear defogger. 5) Select {Work Support} in the «Transmission Diagnosis» display screen of the Subaru Select Monitor. 6) Select {Maintenance mode} in the «Work Support» screen of Subaru Select Monitor.
7) Select {AWD ON/OFF switching mode} in the «Maintenance mode» screen of the Subaru Select Monitor. 8) Follow the messages displayed on the Subaru Select Monitor screen when working.
Switching completes successfully if any of the following messages is displayed.
When switching from AWD to FWD: {Switched to FF. To return to AWD, perform basic mode again.} When switching from FWD to AWD: {Switched to AWD. To return to FF, perform basic mode again.}

NOTE:

• If communication error occurs during switching mode, start in the “AWD ON/OFF switching mode” again. • If operation is interrupted before the successful end message is displayed, perform the {AWD ON/OFF switching mode} from the beginning until confirming the operation is successfully ended. If this mode fails to complete successfully, the cause is as follows.

Select lever is not in “P” range. Engine is running. For detailed operation procedures, refer to “PC application help for Subaru Select Monitor”.

### 1. GENERAL PRECAUTION

Road tests should be conducted to properly diagnose the condition of CVT.

CAUTION: Always observe the local traffic laws when performing the test.

### 2. D RANGE SHIFT FUNCTION

Make sure the engine speed is 1,100 — 1,300 rpm while driving on the level road at 50 km/h (31 MPH) after accelerating from halting to 1/4 of accelerator opening angle. Then stop the vehicle. Check normal gear change has occurred while the vehicle speed changes from a constant speed to zero.

### 3. KICK-DOWN FUNCTION

Check if engine speed will rise by operating the accelerator opening angle to the full from a constant speed of 50 km/h (31 MPH) or more.

### 4. ENGINE BRAKE OPERATION

Model with manual mode

• Drive in “6th speed of manual mode” [70 — 80 km/h (43 — 50 MPH)], and shift down from 6th to 5th. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches “6”  “5”. At the same time, check the engine brake in 5th gear. • Drive in “5th speed of manual mode” [60 — 70 km/h (37 — 43 MPH)], and shift down from 5th to 4th. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches “5”  “4”. At the same time, check the engine brake in 4th gear. • Drive in “4th speed of manual mode” [50 — 60 km/h (31 — 37 MPH)], and shift down from 4th to 3rd. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches “4”  “3”. At the same time, check the engine brake in 3rd gear. • Drive in “3rd speed of manual mode” [40 — 50 km/h (25 — 31 MPH)], and shift down from 3rd to 2nd. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches “3”  “2”. At the same time, check the engine brake in 2nd gear.
• Drive in “2nd speed of manual mode” [20 — 30 km/h (12 — 19 MPH)], and shift down from 2nd to 1st. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches “2”  “1”. At the same time, check the engine brake in 1st gear.

### Model without manual mode

Drive in D range at [50 — 60 km/h (31 — 37 MPH)], and shift to “L” range. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches “D”  “L”. At the same time, check the engine brake in L range.

### 5. LOCK-UP FUNCTION

When the accelerator is lightly depressed while driving on a flat road in “D” range, check that rpm does not change abruptly.

### 6. P RANGE OPERATION

Stop the vehicle on an uphill grade of 5% or more and shift to the “P” range and apply the parking brake.
Check that the vehicle does not move when the parking brake is released.

### 7. NOISE AND VIBRATION

Check for noise and vibration during driving at a constant speed, accelerating, decelerating and manual shif operation.

### 8. OIL LEAKAGE

After the driving test, inspect for leakage of CVTF and differential gear oil from the transmission body.

### A: INSPECTION

CAUTION: Make sure no other person is around the vehicle during stall test measurement.

NOTE:

Stall test is extremely important in diagnosing the condition of CVT and engine. The test is necessary to measure the engine stall speeds in “R” and “D” range.

Purposes of the stall test:

Operational check of forward clutch and reverse brake Operational check of the torque converter assembly • Engine performance check 1) Place wheel chocks at the front and rear of all wheels and engage the parking brake. 2) Turn the A/C OFF. 3) Using the Subaru Select Monitor, check if the throttle valve operates when you depress the accelerator pedal. <Ref. to EN(H4DO)(diag)-41, DISPLAY OF ENGINE FREEZE FRAME DATA, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.> 4) Check the engine oil level. <Ref. to LU(H4DO)-13, Engine Oil.> 5) Check the coolant level. <Ref. to CO(H4DO)-14, Engine Coolant.> 6) Adjust the CVTF level. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-35, ADJUSTMENT, CVTF.> 7) Increase the CVTF temperature to 60 — 80°C (140 — 176°F) with the engine running and the select lever shifted to “N” or “P” range. 8) Shift the select lever to “D” range. 9) Depress the accelerator pedal to the full while fully depressing the foot brake pedal with your left foot. 10) When the engine speed stabilizes, quickly record the engine speed and release accelerator pedal. Shift the select lever to “N” range. Let the engine idle for one minute or more to cool it down.

### Stall Test

11) Shift to “R” range and perform the same stall test.

NOTE:

• Do not perform a stall test for over 5 seconds at a time. (From closed throttle, fully open throttle to stall speed reading.) Failure to follow this instruction will cause the engine oil and CVTF to deteriorate and the clutch and brake to be adversely affected.
• Be sure to cool down the engine for at least one minute after each stall test with the select lever set in the “P” or “N” range and with the idle speed of 1,200 rpm or less.
• If the stall speed is higher than the specified range, attempt to finish the stall test in as short a time as possible, in order to prevent the CVT from sustaining damage.

Stall speed standard: D range: 2,000 — 2,700 rpm R range: 1,900 — 2,600 rpm

### A: INSPECTION

NOTE:

When the select lever is shifted while the engine is idling, there will be a certain time elapse or lag before
shock is felt. This symptom helps to check the condition of forward clutch and reverse brake.
• Perform the test at normal operation CVTF temperature of 60 — 80°C (140 — 176°F). Be sure to allow one minute or more interval between tests. Make three measurements and take the average value.
1) Apply the parking brake.
2) Start the engine. Check the idle speed. (A/C OFF)
3) Shift the select lever from “N” to “D” range. Using a stop watch, measure the time elapsed from shifting the
lever until the shock is felt.

### Time lag standard:

1.5 seconds or less

If “N”  “D” time lag is longer than specified:

Secondary pressure (line pressure) is too low. Forward clutch worn Forward clutch piston malfunction Control valve body malfunction
• Learning incomplete
4) In the same manner, measure the time lag when shifting from “N” range to “R” range.

Time lag standard: 1.5 seconds or less

If “N”  “R” time lag is longer than specified:

Secondary pressure (line pressure) is too low. Reverse brake worn
Reverse brake piston malfunction
Control valve body malfunction
Learning incomplete

### 8. Secondary Pressure (Line Pressure) Test

A: INSPECTION

CAUTION:

• Directly after the vehicle has been running or the engine has been idling for a long time, the CVTF is hot. Be careful not to burn yourself.

Make sure no other person is around the vehicle during secondary pressure (line pressure) test measurement.

After performing the secondary pressure (line pressure) test measurement, adjust the CVTF level.

NOTE:

If the pulley and variator chain, clutch or brake show signs of slipping or shift feel is not correct, check the secondary pressure (line pressure). • Connect Subaru Select Monitor to vehicle so as to measure the engine speed and actual secondary pressure (secondary pressure (line pressure)). • In many cases, slippage or inability to operate the vehicle may be due to insufficient oil pressure for the operation of clutch, brake or control valve. 1) Lift up the vehicle. 2) Remove the secondary pressure (line pressure) test plug, and install ST1 and ST2.

### Removal of the test plug and installation of the ST shall be both performed quickly.

NOTE:

Use ST2 PRESSURE GAUGE ADAPTER with genuine O-ring (part No. 806916050) attached. ST1 18801AA000 OIL PRESSURE GAUGE ASSY
ST2 18681AA010 PRESSURE GAUGE ADAPTER

![](images/242e4d6438e66e1d51aba24ea97018c09a58fc6ab5498fec275ca8320555a8f2.jpg)
(A) O-ring (genuine part)

3) Lower the vehicle.

aru Select Monitor, check if the throttle valve operates when you depress the accelerator pedal. <Ref. to EN(H4DO)(diag)-41, DISPLAY OF ENGINE FREEZE FRAME DATA, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.>
6) Check the engine oil level. <Ref. to LU(H4DO)-13, Engine Oil.>
7) Check the coolant level. <Ref. to CO(H4DO)-14, Engine Coolant.>
8) Adjust the CVTF level. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-35, ADJUSTMENT, CVTF.>
9) Increase the CVTF temperature to 60 — 80°C (140 — 176°F) with the engine running and the select lever shifted to “N” or “P” range.
10) Shift the select lever to “D” range.
11) Depress the accelerator pedal to the full while fully depressing the foot brake pedal with your left foot. 12) Immediately after the engine speed becomes steady, record the reading of the secondary pressure (line pressure), engine speed and actual secondary pressure on Subaru Select Monitor. And then release the accelerator pedal. Shift the select lever to “N” range. Let the engine idle for one minute or more to cool it down.

NOTE:

• Do not continue the stall test for 5 seconds or more at a time (from fully closed throttle, fully open throttle to secondary pressure (line pressure) reading). Failure to follow this instruction will cause the engine oil and CVTF to deteriorate and the clutch and brake to be adversely affected.
• After performing the secondary pressure (line pressure) test, be sure to cool down the engine for at least one minute with the select lever set in “P” or “N” range and with the idle speed at 1 ,200 rpm or less. • Under each condition, check that the measured pressure matches almost totally with actual secondary pressure.
• When both measured pressure and actual secondary pressure are out of specification, judge as control valve malfunction.
• The value at stall is for reference because the pressure changes under different conditions or circumstances.

The value at idling is steady because it is not affected by any condition or circumstance.
